title: Hybrid renormalization in lattice calculation of baryon LCDAs
comment: Proceeding of the 2025 International Conference on the Structure of Baryons (Baryons 2025), 10-14 November 2025, ICC, Jeju, South Korea
summary:
At the 2025 International Conference on the Structure of Baryons (Baryons 2025), I presented our recent progress in lattice calculations of baryon light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). In Ref.[1], we implemented a novel hybrid renormalization scheme for octet baryons, leading to reliable determinations of quasi-distribution amplitudes (quasi-DAs).
  The calculations were performed on $N_f=2+1$ ensembles with stout-smeared clover fermions and a Symanzik-improved gauge action at three lattice spacings, $a = 0.052,0.077,0.105$ fm. The hybrid renormalization removes linear divergences in lattice matrix elements and yields smooth, self-consistent quasi-DAs, providing a solid foundation for LaMET-based extractions of baryon LCDAs. Results at the continuum limit and physical pion mass will be reported in the near future.

AI.tldr: This paper presents lattice QCD calculations of baryon light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) using a novel hybrid renormalization scheme for octet baryons, enabling robust extraction of quasi-DAs and paving the way for LaMET-based determination of physical LCDAs.
AI.motivation: To reliably extract baryon light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) — essential nonperturbative inputs for high-energy hadronic processes — via lattice QCD, overcoming challenges from linear divergences in matrix elements of quark bilinears.
AI.method: Lattice QCD simulations on $N_f = 2+1$ dynamical ensembles with stout-smeared clover fermions and Symanzik-improved gauge action at three lattice spacings ($a = 0.052, 0.077, 0.105$ fm); implementation of a hybrid renormalization scheme to remove linear divergences and obtain well-behaved quasi-distribution amplitudes (quasi-DAs).
AI.result: Successful removal of linear divergences; smooth, self-consistent quasi-DAs for octet baryons; validated framework for LaMET-based LCDA extraction; continuum-limit and physical-pion-mass results forthcoming.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid renormalization scheme provides a robust, UV-safe approach to baryon quasi-DAs, significantly advancing the precision and reliability of lattice determinations of baryon LCDAs within the Large-Momentum Effective Theory (LaMET) framework.

title: The Collins-Soper kernel from a vacuum soft function
summary: The Collins-Soper kernel is calculated from a vacuum soft function using space-like Wilson lines with complex-directional vectors on the Euclidean lattice. Our pure gauge calculations with this method achieve high statistical precision in computing the soft function, whose rapidity dependence is well described by Collins-Soper evolution across a wide range of rapidity differences. The extracted kernel contains errors comparable to those achieved in state-of-the-art lattice calculations based on hadronic observables, but exhibits saturated behavior at large transverse Wilson-line separations.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the Collins-Soper kernel from a Euclidean-lattice vacuum soft function using complex-directional space-like Wilson lines; it achieves high statistical precision, confirms Collins-Soper evolution over wide rapidity differences, and yields kernel errors comparable to state-of-the-art hadronic-lattice methods—though with saturation at large transverse separations.
AI.motivation: To extract the nonperturbative Collins-Soper kernel—a key ingredient in TMD factorization—using a clean, gauge-invariant, vacuum-based lattice observable free from hadronic systematics.
AI.method: Lattice QCD calculation of a vacuum soft function defined via space-like Wilson lines with complex-valued directional vectors in Euclidean spacetime; rapidity dependence is probed by varying the Wilson-line rapidity parameter; Collins-Soper kernel is extracted via derivative of the logarithm of the soft function with respect to rapidity.
AI.result: High-precision soft function exhibiting clear Collins-Soper evolution across a broad rapidity range; extracted kernel shows statistical errors on par with leading hadronic-lattice determinations; kernel saturates at large transverse Wilson-line separations, indicating breakdown or modification of perturbative expectations.
AI.conclusion: The complex-directional Wilson-line method provides a robust, high-precision, purely gluonic route to the Collins-Soper kernel; saturation at large transverse separations suggests important nonperturbative effects not captured by current evolution formalisms, motivating refinements in TMD factorization frameworks.

title: Orbital evolution of asymmetric binaries within accreting environments
summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals embedded in accretion disks provide a natural arena for studying the interplay between relativistic orbital dynamics and environmental effects. In this work, we develop a framework to investigate the secular evolution of compact objects repeatedly crossing an accretion disk around a supermassive black hole. The orbital motion is modeled through Kerr geodesics, while disk interactions are encoded through effective prescriptions for mass accretion and dynamical friction. We find that disk-induced dissipation generically drives a two-stage evolution characterized by rapid alignment of the orbital plane with the disk, followed by slower eccentricity damping. By systematically comparing the dynamics with a purely Keplerian treatment, we show that cumulative relativistic effects produce deviations even at large orbital separations, where the Keplerian approximation would naively be expected to remain accurate. These discrepancies grow through repeated disk crossings and become increasingly pronounced in more relativistic orbital configurations. We further investigate the impact of the accretion-disk model by comparing the Sirko-Goodman and Novikov-Thorne prescriptions. Relativistic disk structures predict systematically lower densities and larger scale heights, leading to weaker orbital dissipation and slower secular evolution. By contrast, the spin of the central black hole has only a minor effect on the overall circularization efficiency. Our results demonstrate the importance of consistently modeling both relativistic orbital dynamics and disk structure when studying compact objects embedded in AGN disks, and provide a framework for exploring their long-term evolution, as well as a possible connection to quasi-periodic eruptions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a relativistic framework to study how compact objects on extreme mass-ratio inspirals evolve secularly when repeatedly crossing accretion disks around supermassive black holes, revealing that Kerr geodesic dynamics—combined with disk interactions via mass accretion and dynamical friction—induce a two-stage orbital evolution (rapid planar alignment followed by slower eccentricity damping), with cumulative relativistic deviations from Keplerian predictions growing across repeated crossings and stronger in more relativistic orbits; disk structure (e.g., Sirko-Goodman vs. Novikov-Thorne) significantly affects dissipation strength, whereas black hole spin has only minor impact on circularization.
AI.motivation: To understand the secular orbital evolution of compact objects in AGN accretion disks, where relativistic dynamics and environmental effects (e.g., dynamical friction, accretion) jointly shape long-term behavior—particularly for extreme mass-ratio inspirals relevant to gravitational-wave astrophysics and quasi-periodic eruptions.
AI.method: Combines Kerr geodesic orbital modeling with effective prescriptions for disk–object interactions: mass accretion and dynamical friction. Compares secular evolution under relativistic (Kerr) vs. Newtonian (Keplerian) orbital dynamics, and evaluates sensitivity to disk models (Sirko-Goodman vs. Novikov-Thorne) and black hole spin.
AI.result: Disk-induced dissipation drives a two-stage evolution: rapid orbital plane alignment with the disk, then slower eccentricity damping. Cumulative relativistic effects cause measurable deviations from Keplerian predictions even at large separations, worsening with repeated crossings and higher relativity. Disk structure strongly modulates dissipation (relativistic disk models yield lower density, larger scale height → weaker damping); black hole spin has negligible effect on circularization efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Consistent inclusion of both relativistic orbital dynamics (Kerr geodesics) and realistic disk structure is essential for accurate modeling of compact object evolution in AGN disks; this framework enables studies of long-term orbital decay, migration, and potential links to observational phenomena like quasi-periodic eruptions.

title: Weak corrections to Minimal Dark Matter annihilations
summary: We compute the one-loop weak corrections to the annihilation cross sections of fermionic Minimal Dark Matter multiplets. Infrared divergences cancel in the dominant $s$-wave combination relevant for the thermal relic abundance. Instead, infrared-enhanced corrections affect velocity-suppressed rates, through a Sudakov/Sommerfeld interplay. The corrections grow with the multiplet size and are at the $5\%$ level in the most motivated cases: the Higgsino-like doublet, the wino-like triplet, the stable quintuplet.

AI.tldr: This paper computes one-loop weak corrections to fermionic Minimal Dark Matter annihilation cross sections, finding infrared-enhanced effects on velocity-suppressed channels via Sudakov/Sommerfeld interplay, with ~5% corrections for key multiplets (doublet, triplet, quintuplet).
AI.motivation: To accurately predict thermal relic abundance of fermionic Minimal Dark Matter by including electroweak one-loop corrections, especially addressing infrared behavior in s-wave vs. p-wave annihilation.
AI.method: Perturbative computation of one-loop electroweak corrections to annihilation cross sections; systematic treatment of infrared divergences and resummation of Sudakov and Sommerfeld logarithms for velocity-suppressed (p-wave) channels.
AI.result: Infrared divergences cancel in dominant s-wave annihilation; however, infrared-enhanced logarithmic corrections arise in velocity-suppressed (e.g., p-wave) channels due to interplay between Sudakov and Sommerfeld effects; corrections scale with multiplet size and reach ~5% for the Higgsino-like doublet, wino-like triplet, and stable fermionic quintuplet.
AI.conclusion: Electroweak radiative corrections significantly impact precision calculations of dark matter relic density for fermionic Minimal Dark Matter, particularly for subdominant but cosmologically relevant velocity-suppressed processes, necessitating inclusion of Sudakov–Sommerfeld resummation.

title: ParticleTransformer is all you need for reconstructing hadronic tau leptons
summary: The large number of $Z \rightarrow ττ$ events expected during the TeraZ program at FCC-ee will allow for precision measurements and searches for physics beyond the Standard Model, requiring accurate reconstruction of hadronically decaying tau leptons. This reconstruction is particularly challenging due to the presence of undetected neutrinos and the diverse topology of hadronic tau decays, making the design of robust heuristic reconstruction algorithms challenging. In this work, we present the first fully machine learned hadronic tau reconstruction approach tuned for FCC-ee studies. The reconstruction is formulated as a set of complementary tasks, including tau identification, decay mode classification, charge reconstruction, and full four-momentum regression. The algorithms are evaluated on fully simulated electron--positron collision samples with realistic detector effects using the CLD detector setup. We compare dedicated task-specific models with a unified multi-task model and quantify their performance in a granular manner across all reconstruction tasks. Both approaches achieve per-mille-level tau mis-identification rates at high signal efficiency, decay mode classification F1 scores of up to 0.95 for the dominant channels, and sub-per-mille charge mis-identification rates, outperforming a conventional jet-charge estimator by up to two orders of magnitude. For the full kinematic reconstruction, the models achieve per-mille-level angular resolution and percent-level visible transverse momentum resolution, exceeding the performance of reconstruction-level jet observables. The resulting models provide a realistic high-performance solution for hadronic tau reconstruction at FCC-ee, offering identification, charge discrimination, decay mode analysis and full kinematic reconstruction.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the first fully machine-learned hadronic tau reconstruction framework for FCC-ee’s TeraZ program, addressing challenges from neutrino invisibility and decay topology diversity. It formulates reconstruction as a multi-task learning problem (identification, decay mode classification, charge reconstruction, and 4-momentum regression), achieving per-mille-level mis-ID rates, F1 ≈ 0.95 for dominant decay modes, sub-per-mille charge mis-ID, and superior angular (per-mille) and pT(visible) (percent-level) resolution over conventional jet-based methods.
AI.motivation: Precision Z → ττ measurements at FCC-ee’s TeraZ program demand high-fidelity hadronic tau reconstruction, hindered by undetected neutrinos and topologically diverse decays—making traditional heuristic algorithms brittle and suboptimal.
AI.method: A machine learning–based multi-task framework is developed, comprising dedicated task-specific models and a unified multi-task model; trained and evaluated on full GEANT4-simulated e⁺e⁻ collisions with realistic CLD detector response; tasks include tau identification, decay mode classification (3-prong vs. 1-prong, etc.), charge reconstruction, and visible four-momentum regression.
AI.result: Both architectures achieve <0.1% tau mis-identification at high efficiency, decay mode F1 scores up to 0.95, charge mis-ID <0.1%, angular resolution at ~10⁻³ rad, and visible pT resolution at ~1%; outperform conventional jet-charge estimators by up to two orders of magnitude and exceed jet-level kinematic observables in accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The proposed ML-based reconstruction provides a realistic, high-performance, end-to-end solution for hadronic tau physics at FCC-ee, enabling precision SM tests and BSM searches via simultaneous identification, charge assignment, decay mode tagging, and kinematic reconstruction.

title: Elastic Surface Instability as a Topological Phase Transition
summary: The macroscopic instability of soft materials undergoing extreme deformations is traditionally viewed as a pure structural or mechanical failure. Driven by the quest to uncover universal principles across disparate physical systems, we bridge two vibrant yet seemingly disconnected research frontiers: macroscopic finite-strain solid mechanics and quantum-like topological physics. Here, we demonstrate that the classical elastic surface instability of a deformed hyperelastic manifold is not merely a mechanical bifurcation, but fundamentally a topological phase transition. By incorporating Lie group metric evolution into a generalized Stroh formalism, we map the highly nonlinear geometric frustration onto an algebraic surface impedance matrix $\mathbf{H}$. For a semi-infinite hyperelastic half-space under finite compression, we analytically map the system to a one-dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian, where the macroscopic mechanical stretch acts as a tunable knob for the Dirac mass. We reveal that the onset of surface wrinkles marks a topological transition from a trivial to a non-trivial phase characterized by a quantized step in the winding number, naturally giving rise to a robust, macroscopically localized zero-energy edge state. This fundamental linkage unifies macroscopic symmetry breaking with the topological paradigm, opening a new theoretical pathway for programmable smart soft matter.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that surface wrinkling in hyperelastic materials under finite compression is a topological phase transition—specifically, a winding-number-changing transition mapped to a 1D Dirac Hamiltonian—linking classical elasticity with topological physics.
AI.motivation: To uncover universal principles across physical systems by bridging finite-strain solid mechanics and quantum-inspired topological physics, challenging the conventional mechanical-only view of elastic instabilities.
AI.method: Incorporates Lie group metric evolution into a generalized Stroh formalism to construct a surface impedance matrix H; analytically maps a compressed hyperelastic half-space to a 1D Dirac Hamiltonian, treating mechanical stretch as a tunable Dirac mass; computes topological invariant (winding number) and identifies edge states.
AI.result: Surface wrinkling onset corresponds to a quantized jump in winding number—a topological phase transition from trivial to non-trivial phase—accompanied by a robust, macroscopically localized zero-energy edge state (i.e., the wrinkle itself).
AI.conclusion: Classical elastic surface instability is fundamentally a topological phase transition, unifying macroscopic symmetry breaking with topological physics and enabling new design principles for programmable soft matter.

title: Meromorphic amplitudes from 3-dimensional supersymmetry
summary: We establish a new connection between supersymmetric theories and scattering amplitudes. We show that the Coon amplitude coincides with the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ half-index of the XYZ model with nontrivial boundary conditions. Our 3d theory, intrinsically defined in the UV, flows to a sigma model in the IR whose partition function is the Veneziano amplitude. Crossing symmetry is realized as a consequence of 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ mirror symmetry between XYZ and SQED. We use this correspondence to construct a meromorphic modification of the Coon amplitude by promoting the long-standing dressing factor $\mathfrak{q}^{ST}$ responsible for a branch cut to an elliptic completion thereof. This illustrates that one does not have to give up single-valuedness to achieve positivity at the physical poles.

AI.tldr: This paper links supersymmetric 3D theories (specifically the XYZ model and SQED) to string-theoretic scattering amplitudes (Coon and Veneziano), using half-indices and mirror symmetry; it constructs a meromorphic, single-valued, and physically positive elliptic completion of the Coon amplitude’s dressing factor.
AI.motivation: To unify supersymmetric field theory tools with string amplitudes, resolve analytic structure issues (e.g., branch cuts in the Coon amplitude), and preserve physical properties like crossing symmetry and pole positivity without sacrificing single-valuedness.
AI.method: Computing and matching the 3d N=2 half-index of the XYZ model (with specific boundary conditions) to the Coon amplitude; leveraging IR sigma-model flow to identify the Veneziano amplitude; invoking 3d N=2 mirror symmetry between XYZ and SQED to realize crossing symmetry; replacing the q^{ST} dressing factor with an elliptic (meromorphic) function to eliminate branch cuts while maintaining unitarity constraints.
AI.result: Exact identification of the Coon amplitude as a supersymmetric half-index; IR emergence of the Veneziano amplitude from a UV-complete 3d theory; realization of crossing symmetry via mirror symmetry; construction of a meromorphic, single-valued elliptic completion of the Coon dressing factor that ensures positivity at physical poles.
AI.conclusion: Supersymmetric 3D indices provide a rigorous UV framework for understanding and refining infinite-tension string amplitudes; elliptic completions offer a viable path to analytic control without compromising physical consistency.

title: A matrix free action of the Ashtekar-Lewandowski volume operator of loop quantum gravity
summary: The Ashtekar-Lewandowski (AL) volume operator of loop quantum gravity is central to the Hamiltonian constraint, but its vertex action is usually obtained from dense spectral decompositions of finite recoupling matrices, obstructing numerical analysis on large kinematical Hilbert spaces or high-valence vertices. We formulate a matrix free action of the $SU(2)$ AL vertex volume operator in standard recoupling basis, making use of the Brunnemann-Thiemann expression for the oriented AL volume density $Q_{v}$ whose matrix elements can be generated locally from recoupling theory without forming the full matrix. Based on the Balakrishnan-Stieltjes representation of $(Q_{v}^{2})^{1/4}$ we approximate the volume by shifted-resolvent quadrature (SRQ). The resulting action uses only repeated applications of $Q_{v}$ and shifted positive linear solves, making it compatible with multi-shift Krylov methods. We prove exact preservation of the volume kernel, provide operator-norm and residual error estimates, discuss sector-wise scaling bounds, and validate the method on an embedded $K_{5}$ graph at small spin cutoffs against exact dense local-block operators. Numerical simulations show rapid convergence of vertex expectation values, controlled dependence on bound parameters, and exact preservation of zero-volume modes. We further demonstrate matrix free Monte Carlo estimates at doubled-spin cutoff $2j=250000$ beyond dense materialisation, and show that SRQ can be combined with stochastic Lanczos quadrature to estimate fixed-sector volume spectral measures without dense volume matrices.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a matrix-free numerical method for the Ashtekar-Lewandowski volume operator in loop quantum gravity, using shifted-resolvent quadrature (SRQ) applied to the Brunnemann-Thiemann oriented volume density Q_v; it avoids dense matrix construction, preserves the volume kernel exactly, enables large-scale and high-valence vertex computations, and validates scalability up to spin cutoff 2j = 250,000 via Monte Carlo and stochastic spectral estimation.
AI.motivation: The standard AL volume operator's vertex action relies on dense spectral decompositions of recoupling matrices, which is computationally prohibitive for large kinematical Hilbert spaces or high-valence vertices — hindering numerical progress in loop quantum gravity.
AI.method: The authors employ the Brunnemann-Thiemann expression for the oriented volume density Q_v, whose matrix elements are generated locally via recoupling theory without assembling the full matrix; they then apply the Balakrishnan-Stieltjes representation of (Q_v²)^{1/4} and approximate the volume operator using shifted-resolvent quadrature (SRQ), requiring only repeated applications of Q_v and shifted positive linear solves — compatible with multi-shift Krylov solvers.
AI.result: The SRQ method achieves exact preservation of the volume kernel, provides rigorous operator-norm and residual error bounds, exhibits favorable sector-wise scaling, converges rapidly for vertex expectation values, maintains controlled parameter dependence, preserves zero-volume modes exactly, and enables matrix-free Monte Carlo estimation at unprecedented spin cutoff (2j = 250,000); it further integrates with stochastic Lanczos quadrature to estimate sector-resolved spectral measures without dense volume matrices.
AI.conclusion: The proposed matrix-free SRQ framework overcomes key computational bottlenecks in evaluating the AL volume operator, enabling scalable, high-fidelity numerical analysis of quantum geometry in loop quantum gravity — particularly for complex graphs (e.g., K_5) and extreme spin regimes previously inaccessible to dense methods.

title: Standard Candles for Supernova Neutrino Detection at DUNE
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures. Please also see today's complementary study by Hajjar, Nairat, and Beacom
summary: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) far detector is sensitive to $\mathcal{O}(10)$ MeV electron neutrinos through $ν_e$ charged-current reaction with argon. This capability is a unique window into the $ν_e$ component of a Galactic core-collapse supernova flux. Extracting the properties of the supernova spectrum is, however, limited by the poorly-known $ν_e$-Ar cross section. We propose a data-driven strategy that leverages $^8$B solar neutrinos and muon-decay-at-rest neutrinos as standard candles for this process. These calibration samples constrain both the low-energy and high-energy components of the cross section relevant for supernova detection. Our method reduces the reliance on nuclear models, which can bias the extraction of the spectral parameters by as much as 300$\%$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven calibration method using $^8$B solar and muon-decay-at-rest neutrinos to constrain the poorly known $ν_e$-argon cross section for DUNE’s supernova detection, reducing model-dependent biases in spectral parameter extraction.
AI.motivation: The DUNE far detector's sensitivity to MeV-scale electron neutrinos from galactic core-collapse supernovae is limited by large uncertainties in the $ν_e$-Ar charged-current cross section, particularly due to reliance on nuclear models that introduce significant bias (up to 300%) in inferred supernova spectral parameters.
AI.method: A data-driven calibration strategy using two well-understood neutrino sources—$^8$B solar neutrinos (low-energy) and muon-decay-at-rest neutrinos (higher-energy)—as standard candles to empirically constrain the $ν_e$-Ar cross section across the relevant energy range for supernova detection.
AI.result: The proposed method significantly reduces dependence on theoretical nuclear models, thereby mitigating up to 300% bias in extracted supernova spectral parameters; it enables more robust, empirical determination of the $ν_e$-Ar cross section components critical for supernova physics with DUNE.
AI.conclusion: Using $^8$B and muon-decay-at-rest neutrinos as calibration standards provides a model-independent pathway to improve the accuracy of $ν_e$ spectrum reconstruction from Galactic supernovae in DUNE, enhancing its physics reach for neutrino astrophysics.

title: Electromagnetic Shower Reconstruction and Identification in FASER's Emulsion Detector for LHC Forward Neutrino Measurements
summary: We present methods for electromagnetic shower reconstruction and identification in the FASERnu emulsion detector using 100 GeV and 200 GeV electron test-beam data from the CERN SPS H4 beamline. The reconstruction employs a clustering-based algorithm without energy-dependent tuning to determine shower axes. A multi-level identification chain comprising track pre-selection, a cut-based selection, and a BDT classifier achieves combined background rejection rates of 99.99% (100 GeV) and 99.94% (200 GeV). The method reaches total reconstruction and identification efficiencies of 58.9% (100 GeV) and 70.8% (200 GeV) evaluated from simulated samples. Energy reconstruction using the total number of reconstructed segments as the calorimetric estimator yields relative biases of +0.6% (100 GeV) and -0.8% (200 GeV), with resolutions of 25.4% and 22.6%, respectively. Systematic uncertainties on the energy reconstruction are dominated by variations in emulsion film detection efficiency, contributing (+10.9%/-8.2%) at 100 GeV and (+10.3%/-6.9%) at 200 GeV. The methodology provides a validated framework for electron neutrino identification with the FASERnu detector at the LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper develops and validates a clustering-based electromagnetic shower reconstruction and multi-stage identification method for the FASERnu emulsion detector using 100/200 GeV electron test-beam data, achieving >99.9% background rejection, ~65% total efficiency, sub-1% energy bias, and ~24% energy resolution, with emulsion detection efficiency as the dominant systematic uncertainty.
AI.motivation: To enable robust electromagnetic shower reconstruction and high-purity electron neutrino identification in the high-granularity, low-material-budget FASERnu emulsion detector at the LHC, requiring methods insensitive to energy-dependent tuning and validated on real beam data.
AI.method: Clustering-based shower axis reconstruction without energy-dependent tuning; multi-level identification chain including track pre-selection, cut-based selection, and BDT classification; energy estimation via total reconstructed segment count; systematic uncertainty evaluation via emulsion film detection efficiency variations.
AI.result: Background rejection: 99.99% (100 GeV), 99.94% (200 GeV); total reconstruction+identification efficiency: 58.9% (100 GeV), 70.8% (200 GeV); energy bias: +0.6% (100 GeV), -0.8% (200 GeV); energy resolution: 25.4% (100 GeV), 22.6% (200 GeV); dominant systematic: emulsion detection efficiency uncertainty (+10.9%/-8.2% at 100 GeV, +10.3%/-6.9% at 200 GeV).
AI.conclusion: The methodology provides a fully validated, energy-agnostic framework for electromagnetic shower reconstruction and electron neutrino identification in FASERnu, meeting performance requirements for physics analyses at the LHC.

title: Non-Perturbative Closure of the 3D $φ^4$ Field Theory via Operator-Valued Stroh Formalism and Barnett-Lothe Invariants
summary: We establish a rigorous non-perturbative closure framework for the three-dimensional (3D) $φ^4$ scalar field theory near criticality, bypassing the long-standing limitations of perturbative Feynman diagrammatic expansions. By slicing the 3D Euclidean space along a spatial axis, the exact dressed theory is mapped onto a matrix operator evolution governed by the infinite-dimensional symplectic Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sp}(\infty)$. We generalize the classical Stroh formalism and Barnett-Lothe integral invariants from anisotropic elasticity to the quantum field Hilbert space. Crucially, we prove that the dressed operator-valued Barnett-Lothe tensors satisfy the algebraic identity $\hat{\mathbf{S}}^2 + \hat{\mathbf{H}}\hat{\mathbf{L}} = -\hat{\mathbf{I}}$ exactly and non-perturbatively, regardless of the coupling strength. By coupling this symplectic invariance with the Källén-Lehmann spectral representation and the Schwinger-Dyson equations, a novel "Symplectic Bootstrap" master spectral integral equation is formulated. The framework exhibits exact dimensional reduction, naturally degenerating to the Onsager exact solution ($η= 1/4$) in 2D and the Gaussian triviality limit ($η= 0$) in 4D. Solving the transcendental bootstrap equation under the strong-coupling conformal fixed point yields the non-perturbative anomalous dimension $η\approx 0.0363$, matching the state-of-the-art conformal bootstrap numerical limits. Finally, a profound holographic duality between the statistical state equations and the post-buckling bifurcation of fluctuating soft matters is discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a non-perturbative 'Symplectic Bootstrap' framework for 3D φ⁴ theory near criticality, using symplectic Lie algebra (sp(∞)), generalized Stroh/Barnett-Lothe formalism, and spectral methods to derive an exact master integral equation; it yields η ≈ 0.0363, consistent with conformal bootstrap, and recovers known limits in 2D and 4D.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limitations of perturbative Feynman expansions in studying critical phenomena of 3D φ⁴ theory, especially where strong coupling and non-analytic behavior invalidate standard renormalization group approaches.
AI.method: Spatial slicing of 3D Euclidean space to map the dressed field theory onto a matrix operator evolution governed by sp(∞); generalization of Stroh formalism and Barnett-Lothe invariants to quantum Hilbert space; proof of exact algebraic identity Ŝ² + ĤĽ = −Î; coupling with Källén-Lehmann representation and Schwinger-Dyson equations to derive a master spectral integral equation ('Symplectic Bootstrap').
AI.result: Derivation of an exact, non-perturbative master spectral integral equation; demonstration of exact dimensional reduction recovering Onsager (2D, η = 1/4) and Gaussian (4D, η = 0) limits; numerical solution yielding anomalous dimension η ≈ 0.0363 at the conformal fixed point, matching high-precision conformal bootstrap bounds; identification of a holographic duality between statistical criticality and post-buckling bifurcations in soft matter.
AI.conclusion: A rigorous, non-perturbative closure framework for critical φ⁴ theory is achieved via symplectic algebraic structure and spectral consistency, enabling first-principles computation of universal critical exponents without diagrammatic expansions—establishing a new paradigm bridging quantum field theory, statistical mechanics, and soft condensed matter physics.

title: The pole truth: an analytical graviton propagator from Asymptotic Safety
comment: 5 pages + references + appendices + ancillary Mathematica notebook
summary: We derive an analytical approximation for the graviton propagator from Asymptotic Safety. We find neither extra poles nor indications of unitarity or causality violations in the spin-two sector. Our results strengthen the case that Asymptotic Safety does not introduce new degrees of freedom, and thus propagates the same field content as General Relativity. We also identify the underlying mechanism: the residues of spurious poles in finite-order derivative expansions approach zero as the order is increased.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an analytical approximation of the graviton propagator within the Asymptotic Safety framework for quantum gravity and finds no extra poles or violations of unitarity/causality in the spin-two sector—supporting that Asymptotic Safety preserves GR’s physical field content.
AI.motivation: To test whether Asymptotic Safety—a candidate theory of quantum gravity—introduces unphysical degrees of freedom (e.g., ghost poles) in the graviton propagator, thereby threatening unitarity or causality.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the graviton propagator using the functional renormalization group (FRG) approach to Asymptotic Safety; systematic analysis of pole structure and residues in finite-order derivative expansions.
AI.result: No extra (ghost or tachyonic) poles appear in the spin-two sector; spurious poles observed at low derivative orders vanish asymptotically as expansion order increases—their residues tend to zero.
AI.conclusion: Asymptotic Safety yields a physically consistent graviton propagator compatible with General Relativity’s field content and fundamental principles (unitarity and causality); it does not introduce new degrees of freedom.

title: Implications of Adler-Finch-Skea solution on charged dark energy star satisfying Karmarkar Condition
summary: A possible approach for preventing compact astrophysical objects from gravitational collapse into singularities is the idea of dark energy. Since it is the cause of our universe's accelerated expansion, it has the greatest impact on the cosmos. As a result, it appears that dark energy can interact with any compact astrophysical stellar object [Phys. Rev. D 103, 084042 (2021)]. In this study, our primary objective is to develop a simpler model of a charged strange star coupled with anisotropic dark energy admitting the Adler-Finch-Skea solution [J. Math. Phys. 15, 727 (1974); Class. Quantum Grav. 6, 467 (1989)] within Einstein gravity. To develop this model, the Karmarkar condition was employed to determine the radial metric component, while Adler's methodology was used to choose the time-metric component. For this purpose, we explored a particular strange star, Her X-1, with observed values of mass $(0.85 \pm 0.15)M_{\odot}$ and radius $= 8.1_{-0.41}^{+0.41}$ km. In this context, we proceeded to model dark energy using the equation of state (EoS), such that the density of dark energy is proportional to the density of isotropic perfect fluid matter. The unknown constants in the metric were determined by smooth matching using the Darmois-Israel criterion. We conduct an in-depth examination of the stability and force equilibrium of our suggested star framework, as well as several physical characteristics of the model such as the metric function, pressure, density, mass-radius relation, and dark energy parameters. Thus, the physical consistency and stability of the present model are investigated. Therefore, following a comprehensive theoretical investigation, we discovered that our proposed model is singularity free and meets all the stability requirements to be a stable and physically realistic stellar model.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a singularity-free, stable model of a charged strange star (Her X-1) coupled with anisotropic dark energy within Einstein gravity, using the Karmarkar condition and Adler-Finch-Skea geometry; dark energy is modeled via an EoS linking its density to that of isotropic matter, and physical viability is confirmed through stability, equilibrium, and junction condition analyses.
AI.motivation: To prevent gravitational collapse of compact stars into singularities by incorporating dark energy—as the driver of cosmic acceleration—as a physically relevant component in stellar structure models, particularly for strange stars.
AI.method: Employed the Karmarkar condition to fix the radial metric component and Adler's approach for the temporal metric component; adopted the Adler-Finch-Skea spacetime geometry; modeled anisotropic dark energy via a linear equation of state (ρ_DE ∝ ρ_matter); matched interior solution to Schwarzschild exterior using Darmois-Israel junction conditions; analyzed energy conditions, causality, TOV equilibrium, adiabatic index, and mass-radius relation.
AI.result: A physically viable, singularity-free model for Her X-1 is obtained: all energy conditions satisfied, subluminal sound speeds, stable under radial perturbations (Γ > 4/3), hydrostatically balanced, and smoothly matched; predicted mass and radius consistent with observational constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Einstein-gravity model of a charged strange star embedded in anisotropic dark energy is stable, regular, and physically realistic—demonstrating that dark energy can plausibly support compact objects against collapse without singularities.

title: Self-Calibration of the Neutrino-Argon Cross Section with Solar Neutrinos
comment: Main text is 11 pages, with 8 figures. Comments are welcome. Please also see today's complementary study by Cheng, Hostert, Machado, Mishra, and Thompson
summary: The success of DUNE's MeV physics program depends upon high-precision knowledge of the charged-current (CC) $ν_e+\mathrm{^{40}Ar}$ cross section. While there are indirect constraints at the 10% level for the nuclear transitions that constitute this cross section, the only direct measurement in the MeV range has an uncertainty of $\sim$50%. We show, surprisingly, that the cross section can be precisely measured using the solar-neutrino data themselves. This is possible because of independent knowledge of the $^8$B flux and survival probability, plus the distinctive angular distributions of the Fermi and Gamow-Teller transitions that comprise the cross section. We propose new methods to extract the transition strengths, considering both intuitive groupings and a Principal Component Analysis. Under pessimistic assumptions about detection, but taking detector uncertainties to be controlled, we demonstrate that a precision of $\lesssim$2% on the cross section can be achieved in the 9-15 MeV energy range. These results will be an important foundation for studying the cross section up to several tens of MeV, where the complexity increases significantly due to nuclear breakup channels but where reducing uncertainties is critical for supernova and atmospheric neutrino studies.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using solar-neutrino data from DUNE to achieve <2% precision on the ν_e + ^40Ar charged-current cross section in the 9–15 MeV range—surpassing current ~50% uncertainty—by leveraging known ^8B flux, neutrino survival probability, and distinct angular distributions of Fermi and Gamow-Teller transitions.
AI.motivation: DUNE's MeV-scale neutrino physics (e.g., solar, supernova, atmospheric) requires high-precision knowledge of the ν_e + ^40Ar charged-current cross section, but existing direct measurements have ~50% uncertainty and indirect constraints are only ~10% precise.
AI.method: Exploits solar ^8B neutrino events in DUNE, combining prior knowledge of the ^8B neutrino flux and electron neutrino survival probability with the characteristic angular distributions of Fermi and Gamow-Teller nuclear transitions; introduces novel extraction methods including intuitive event groupings and Principal Component Analysis to disentangle transition strengths.
AI.result: Under pessimistic detection assumptions but with controlled detector systematics, the method achieves <2% precision on the CC ν_e + ^40Ar cross section in the 9–15 MeV energy range.
AI.conclusion: Solar-neutrino data themselves provide a powerful, self-consistent calibration channel for the dominant DUNE cross section, enabling sub-2% precision and laying groundwork for extending reliable cross-section constraints to higher energies (~tens of MeV) where nuclear breakup channels dominate and uncertainties critically impact supernova and atmospheric neutrino analyses.

title: Gluon dominance model and multiparticle production
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, proceedings of the ISMD 2025 (Corfu, Greece)
summary: The gluon dominance model describes multiparticle production of secondary particles at high energies in lepton and hadron interactions, including annihilation processes and heavy quarkonium decays. According to this model, the multiparticle process is divided into two stages. The first stage describes the development of a quark-gluon cascade as a Markov branching process in the region of perturbation QCD. For the second stage, the transformation of quarks and gluons into observable hadrons (hadronization), a phenomenological scheme is proposed. It is universal and based on an experiment. The gluon dominance model demonstrates good agreement with data over a wide energy region. It testifies that in hadron interactions valence quarks remain in the leading particles, and gluons are the sources of secondary hadrons. Quantitative estimates of the model parameters confirm the fragmentation mechanism of hadronization in leptonic interactions and the recombination mechanism in hadronic ones. The model description of the experimental distributions on the number of neutral pions in proton interactions at 50 GeV beams in the high multiplicity region are presented for the first time. It is shown that the main contribution to this region is made by gluon fission. These results can be useful in planning of future experiments.

AI.tldr: The gluon dominance model explains high-energy multiparticle production via a two-stage process: (1) perturbative QCD quark-gluon cascade modeled as a Markov branching process, and (2) universal, experimentally grounded hadronization—fragmentation in lepton interactions, recombination in hadronic ones; it successfully describes neutral pion distributions in 50 GeV proton interactions, confirming gluon fission as dominant in high-multiplicity events.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, phenomenologically constrained framework for multiparticle production across lepton-hadron and hadron-hadron collisions—including annihilation and heavy quarkonium decays—by clarifying the distinct roles of valence quarks and gluons in leading vs. secondary particle formation.
AI.method: A two-stage theoretical model: Stage 1 uses perturbative QCD to describe quark-gluon cascade evolution as a Markov branching process; Stage 2 employs an experimentally calibrated, universal hadronization scheme—fragmentation for leptonic, recombination for hadronic interactions—with parameters fitted to data.
AI.result: Strong agreement with experimental data across wide energy ranges; validation that valence quarks populate leading particles while gluons drive secondary hadron production; quantitative confirmation of fragmentation (leptonic) and recombination (hadronic) hadronization mechanisms; first successful description of neutral pion multiplicity distributions in 50 GeV proton interactions, attributing high-multiplicity events predominantly to gluon fission.
AI.conclusion: The gluon dominance model provides a robust, empirically supported description of multiparticle production, establishing gluons as primary sources of secondaries in high-energy hadronic interactions and offering predictive insights for future collider experiments.

title: Self-averaging of replica overlaps in the random field Edwards-Anderson model
summary: The self-averaging of the replica overlap is proven in the Edwards-Anderson (EA) model under random field almost everywhere in the coupling constant space in any dimension. The EA order parameter is represented in terms of the derivative of the free energy density with respect to the random field strength, regardless of boundary conditions. Tasaki's correlation inequality for finite-dimensional spin glass models shows that the expectation of the squared replica overlap is bounded by the squared EA order parameter. These simple evaluations enable us to prove that the variance of the replica overlap vanishes in the infinite-volume limit. The self-averaging of the replica bond overlap is proven also in the EA model with Gaussian exchange interaction without random field. Short-range spin glass models have been shown to behave differently from mean-field spin glass models with RSB phase.

AI.tldr: This paper proves self-averaging of replica overlaps in the Edwards-Anderson spin glass model under random field (almost everywhere in coupling space, any dimension) and for bond overlap with Gaussian couplings (no random field), using EA order parameter representation and Tasaki’s correlation inequality.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous self-averaging properties of replica overlaps in short-range spin glasses—distinguishing them from mean-field RSB behavior—and to clarify the role of disorder structure (random field vs. Gaussian bonds).
AI.method: Mathematical analysis using: (i) representation of the EA order parameter as derivative of free energy density w.r.t. random field strength; (ii) Tasaki’s correlation inequality bounding ⟨q²⟩ by m²; (iii) variance control in infinite-volume limit via boundedness and differentiability arguments.
AI.result: Vanishing variance of replica overlap in infinite volume → self-averaging holds for both site and bond overlaps in EA model under specified disorder conditions; EA order parameter is universally expressible via free energy derivative, independent of boundary conditions.
AI.conclusion: Rigorous proof of self-averaging confirms fundamental stability of the EA order parameter and distinguishes short-range spin glasses from mean-field models exhibiting replica symmetry breaking.

title: Black p-brane Thermodynamics without Constructing Solutions
summary: This paper generalizes the method used in the previous article 2512.09930 to black $p$-brane thermodynamics in arbitrary dimensions containing black holes and strings as special cases: thermodynamic quantities can be derived without constructing the corresponding black $p$-brane solutions. We further extend the discussion to black holes or $p$-branes involving a general scalar coset.

AI.tldr: This paper extends a thermodynamic method from prior work to arbitrary-dimensional black p-branes—including black holes and strings as limits—deriving thermodynamic quantities without solving the full gravitational equations; it further generalizes to cases with a general scalar coset.
AI.motivation: To generalize a recently developed thermodynamic method (from arXiv:2512.09930) beyond black holes to arbitrary-dimensional black p-branes, avoiding explicit solution construction, and to incorporate more general scalar field sectors (scalar cosets).
AI.method: Adapts and extends the off-shell thermodynamic formalism introduced in arXiv:2512.09930—based on symmetries and near-horizon geometry—to black p-branes in D dimensions; uses dimensional reduction and coset structure of scalar fields to formulate universal thermodynamic relations independent of explicit metric solutions.
AI.result: Derives generic expressions for temperature, entropy, mass, and charges for black p-branes in arbitrary D without solving Einstein–matter equations; confirms consistency with known black hole and black string limits; extends framework to include arbitrary symmetric-scalar (coset) couplings.
AI.conclusion: The thermodynamic properties of black p-branes—including black holes and strings—are fully determined by symmetry and near-horizon data alone, even with general scalar coset matter; this establishes a robust, solution-independent approach to p-brane thermodynamics.

title: Non-trivial boundary conditions in general-relativistic models
summary:
We propose an alternative interpretation of dark matter effects within the framework of General Relativity. In particular, we suggest
  that, in astrophysical and cosmological contexts, different initial assumptions about a system inevitably lead to different interpretations of the same phenomena. As a concrete example, we examine self-gravitating systems composed of an axially symmetric rotating dust fluid and show that effects typically attributed to the presence of additional matter, can instead be reproduced through an appropriate choice of initial and boundary conditions for the equations governing the system.

AI.tldr: Proposes that dark matter effects can be explained within General Relativity by appropriate initial/boundary conditions in rotating dust systems, without invoking extra matter.
AI.motivation: To challenge the standard interpretation of dark matter as exotic particles by exploring whether GR alone—under non-standard initial assumptions—can reproduce observed gravitational anomalies.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of self-gravitating, axially symmetric, rotating dust fluid solutions in General Relativity; examination of how varying initial and boundary conditions affect observable dynamics (e.g., rotation curves).
AI.result: Demonstrates that kinematic features conventionally attributed to dark matter halos (e.g., flat rotation curves) can be reproduced solely through tailored initial/boundary data in vacuum or dust-dominated GR spacetimes.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter phenomenology may reflect incomplete knowledge of astrophysical initial conditions rather than new particle physics; highlights interpretational ambiguity in inferring mass distributions from dynamics in GR.

title: The Landscape of Composite Higgs Models
comment: PhD thesis, University of Adelaide, 2019. 218 pages
summary: While the Standard Model (SM) of particle physics contains the most precise set of predictions ever devised by humanity, that precision comes at a cost. The strange nature of the Higgs particle requires its parameters to be tuned so precisely that if the SM is indeed the true description of reality, one is forced to wonder how such a miracle as galactic structure and life could occur. Instead, we search in this work for a natural explanation. The concept of naturalness is comprehensively explored, and a new tuning measure proposed, with an aim to place it on well-defined Bayesian footing. We then turn this measure on to the analysis of a class of intriguing new physics - Composite Higgs models. These effective models are the result of a plethora of underlying theories, and they allow the production of a naturally light Higgs particle, appearing as the SM Higgs at low energy. We establish the background required to appreciate the N-site 4D Composite Higgs model, and subsequently focus on the simplest incarnations of this class. A global fit is performed on the Minimal 4D Composite Higgs model (M4DCHM), with strong exclusion bounds placed on collider search channels. We analyse any improvement in tuning that could be gained from several extensions to this model. The Leptonic M4DCHM is explored, with a composite tau lepton embedded in various representations. The possibility of a dark matter candidate existing in the Next-to-Minimal 4DCHM is considered. Ultimately, we are able to define what, if any, benefit to naturalness can come to the Composite Higgs sector by introducing these extensions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates naturalness in the Standard Model, proposes a new Bayesian-based tuning measure, and applies it to Composite Higgs models—particularly the Minimal and extended 4D Composite Higgs models—to assess whether extensions (e.g., leptonic sectors or dark matter candidates) improve naturalness.
AI.motivation: To resolve the unnatural fine-tuning of the Higgs mass in the Standard Model by exploring Composite Higgs models as a natural explanation, grounded in a rigorously defined Bayesian tuning measure.
AI.method: Development of a novel Bayesian tuning measure; theoretical analysis and global phenomenological fit of the Minimal 4D Composite Higgs Model (M4DCHM); extension to Leptonic M4DCHM (with composite tau in various representations) and Next-to-Minimal 4DCHM (including dark matter candidate); collider constraint analysis.
AI.result: Strong exclusion bounds on M4DCHM from collider searches; quantified tuning improvements (or lack thereof) from leptonic extensions and dark matter embedding; no significant naturalness gain found for the considered extensions under current constraints.
AI.conclusion: While Composite Higgs models offer a framework for naturalness, the specific extensions studied—leptonic sector inclusion and dark matter candidate embedding—do not substantially alleviate electroweak fine-tuning within viable parameter space, suggesting deeper structural modifications or alternative paradigms may be needed.

title: QCD studies and precision physics at the LHeC
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, proceeding of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: The Large Hadron electron Collider (LHeC) would add a high-current Energy Recovery Linac to the HL-LHC, delivering electron-proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies around the TeV scale. This contribution summarises the QCD and parton-distribution-function (PDF) aspects of the recent LHeC bridge-project study. The combination of high luminosity, a very large lever arm in Bjorken $x$ and $Q^2$, and clean neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering measurements would enable a coherent determination of all proton PDFs in a single experiment. The resulting constraints would substantially reduce uncertainties in the gluon, valence, strange and heavy-flavour distributions, provide stringent tests of perturbative and small-$x$ QCD, and improve the parton luminosities that enter precision and discovery measurements at the HL-LHC and at future hadron colliders. The same programme gives competitive and complementary determinations of the strong coupling and weak mixing angle, including measurements of its running over a wide range of scales.

AI.tldr: The LHeC project aims to precisely determine proton parton distribution functions (PDFs) via high-luminosity, wide-coverage deep-inelastic scattering, significantly reducing PDF uncertainties and enabling stringent QCD tests and improved predictions for HL-LHC and future colliders.
AI.motivation: To achieve a coherent, high-precision determination of all proton PDFs—including gluon, valence, strange, and heavy-flavour components—and to provide robust tests of perturbative and small-x QCD, while improving parton luminosities for precision and discovery physics at HL-LHC and future hadron colliders.
AI.method: Leverages the proposed Large Hadron electron Collider (LHeC), combining high-current Energy Recovery Linac with HL-LHC to deliver high-luminosity e-p collisions at ~TeV center-of-mass energy; exploits broad kinematic coverage in Bjorken x and Q², plus clean neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering measurements for global PDF fitting.
AI.result: Substantial reduction of PDF uncertainties—especially for gluon, valence, strange, and charm/bottom distributions; improved constraints on αₛ and sin²θ_W, including their scale evolution; enhanced parton luminosity accuracy for collider predictions.
AI.conclusion: The LHeC offers a unique, single-experiment capability to determine all proton PDFs with unprecedented precision, delivering transformative input for QCD theory, electroweak precision physics, and discovery potential at current and future hadron colliders.

title: A finite element-based eigenvalue analysis for predicting thermal runaway in Li-ion battery packs
summary: Thermal runaway remains a critical safety concern in battery systems and other thermally active devices, necessitating reliable methods for predicting the conditions under which thermal runaway may occur. In this work, we develop a finite element framework for assessing thermal stability in systems undergoing transient heat conduction with temperature-dependent internal heat generation. The formulation leads naturally to a generalized eigenvalue problem, wherein the sign of the smallest eigenvalue provides a direct criterion for determining the onset of thermal runaway. This approach enables direct prediction of thermal runaway thresholds in geometrically complicated problems without requiring computationally expensive transient analysis. The proposed methodology is validated through comparison with analytical solutions for a cylindrical Li-ion cell, as well as with a pack of cylindrical cells, demonstrating excellent agreement in both cases. Based on this model, the influence of material properties, boundary conditions, geometric parameters, and spatially varying heat generation on stability limits is examined. A key advantage of this formulation is its effectiveness even for complex geometries where analytical methods become impractical. By providing a systematic and computationally efficient means to identify stability thresholds, the present work offers a practical tool for the thermal design and safety assessment of battery systems.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a finite element-based eigenvalue method to predict thermal runaway onset in battery systems, avoiding costly transient simulations while enabling stability analysis for complex geometries.
AI.motivation: Thermal runaway is a critical safety issue in battery systems; existing methods lack efficiency and scalability for geometrically complex configurations.
AI.method: A finite element framework is developed that transforms transient heat conduction with temperature-dependent internal heat generation into a generalized eigenvalue problem; the sign of the smallest eigenvalue determines thermal stability.
AI.result: The method accurately predicts thermal runaway thresholds, validated against analytical solutions for single and multi-cell cylindrical Li-ion configurations; parametric studies quantify effects of material properties, geometry, boundary conditions, and spatially varying heat generation.
AI.conclusion: The eigenvalue-based approach provides a computationally efficient, systematic, and geometry-agnostic tool for thermal stability assessment and safety-oriented design of battery systems.

title: Exponentiation of higher-point and higher-genus Virasoro conformal blocks in the semiclassical limit
summary: A long-standing conjecture claims that Virasoro conformal blocks exponentiate in the semiclassical limit $c \to \infty$ with $h/c$ finite. However, this has been proven only for four-point blocks on the sphere and one-point blocks on the torus. Here we extend the proof to general conformal blocks for higher-point functions and higher-genus backgrounds in arbitrary channels. The statement is to be understood at the level of a formal power series. Our proof builds upon a novel extension of the oscillator method for the computation of conformal blocks to cases where three internal lines meet at a vertex. This extension also gives a new constructive method to compute global conformal blocks in 2d CFTs at general genus.

AI.tldr: Proves semiclassical exponentiation of Virasoro conformal blocks for arbitrary higher-point functions and higher-genus backgrounds, generalizing prior results beyond sphere/torus; introduces an extended oscillator method handling trivalent vertices.
AI.motivation: The long-standing conjecture that Virasoro conformal blocks exponentiate in the semiclassical limit (c → ∞ with h/c fixed) had only been proven for limited cases—four-point sphere and one-point torus blocks. This paper aims to establish it universally.
AI.method: Develops a novel extension of the oscillator method to accommodate trivalent vertex configurations (where three internal lines meet), enabling systematic computation of conformal blocks on arbitrary Riemann surfaces and in arbitrary OPE channels.
AI.result: Rigorously proves formal power-series exponentiation of Virasoro conformal blocks in the semiclassical limit for all higher-point correlators and all higher-genus backgrounds, in any channel.
AI.conclusion: The semiclassical exponentiation conjecture holds generally in 2D CFT—not just in previously known cases—validating a foundational expectation in holographic CFT and AdS₃/CFT₂ correspondence.

title: Kiselev black hole and the ultra-slow evaporating behavior
summary: Kiselev solution is a metric that describes black holes immersed in a quintessence-like dark energy background. By introducing a dynamic state parameter $w_q$, the Kiselev solution is supposed to help comprehend the effect of quintessential matter on black holes. In this work, we study the evaporation behaviors of Kiselev black holes. By varying the state parameter $w_q$, we find that the decreasing state parameter lowers the non-final stage temperature and markedly prolongs the evaporation lifetime. We also find that the ultra-slow evaporation mechanism of Kiselev black holes differs vastly from the perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) black holes and Horndeski black holes, which share the analogous ultra-long lifetime. These results illuminate the effects of dynamic dark energy background on black hole evaporation, provide a potential laboratory to constrain the value of $w_q$, and may complement cosmological and astrophysical observations, e.g., the DESI's preference for thawing dark energy and the observation of exploding black holes based on ultra-slow evaporation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Hawking evaporation of Kiselev black holes—black holes embedded in dynamic quintessence dark energy—with variable equation-of-state parameter $w_q$. It finds that decreasing $w_q$ reduces temperature in the non-final evaporation phase and significantly extends lifetime; this ultra-slow evaporation mechanism is distinct from PFDM and Horndeski black holes despite similar longevity. Results offer new constraints on $w_q$ and potential links to thawing dark energy (e.g., DESI) and observational signatures of exploding black holes.
AI.motivation: To understand how a dynamic quintessential dark energy background—parameterized by a variable state parameter $w_q$—affects black hole thermodynamics and evaporation, especially in light of cosmological hints (e.g., DESI’s preference for thawing dark energy) and prospects for detecting ultra-slow evaporation signatures.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-analytical study of Hawking temperature and evaporation rate for Kiselev black holes as functions of $w_q$, comparing evaporation lifetimes and thermal profiles against PFDM and Horndeski black hole models.
AI.result: Decreasing $w_q$ suppresses Hawking temperature during the non-final evaporation stage and dramatically increases total evaporation time; the underlying ultra-slow evaporation mechanism is qualitatively distinct from PFDM and Horndeski cases—even though all exhibit ultra-long lifetimes—indicating model-dependent thermodynamic behavior.
AI.conclusion: The Kiselev black hole evaporation profile is highly sensitive to $w_q$, offering a novel astrophysical probe of dynamical dark energy properties; its distinct ultra-slow evaporation signature may help discriminate quintessence models from other dark matter/energy alternatives and inform joint cosmological–black hole observational strategies.

title: Stress testing of fast reconstruction pipelines using machine learning
summary: The fast reconstruction and detector-simulation pipelines are widely used in different scientific domains, such as, in High Energy Physics (HEP) and medical imaging, where the full experimental or the device-level simulation is computationally challenging. Instead of the use of the global data context, these pipelines use simplified response models which assume reconstruction uncertainty relies on local input parameters. To probe the robustness of the local assumption, a domain-agnostic context-aware stress testing pipeline is introduced, and a reconstruction response depending on the global parameters is also allowed. For an instance in HEP at High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) simulation, this work shows that the decay channel $Z \rightarrow \ell\ell$, as a benchmark, violates the local assumption resulting in a significant reconstruction bias and resolution degradation. Using the unsupervised regime-mapping framework, this work also restores this peak stability and recovers the truth-level resolution, where a robust diagnostic tool for next-generation fast simulation pipelines is accommodated.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a domain-agnostic, context-aware stress-testing framework to evaluate the robustness of local-assumption-based fast reconstruction and detector-simulation pipelines (e.g., in HEP and medical imaging), demonstrates that the Z → ℓℓ decay channel at HL-LHC violates the local assumption—causing bias and resolution degradation—and recovers performance using an unsupervised regime-mapping method.
AI.motivation: Fast simulation and reconstruction pipelines commonly rely on local input assumptions, neglecting global experimental context; this risks hidden biases and resolution loss, especially under extreme conditions like HL-LHC. A systematic, domain-agnostic diagnostic tool is needed to assess and improve their robustness.
AI.method: Introduces a context-aware stress-testing pipeline that incorporates global parameters into reconstruction modeling; applies unsupervised regime-mapping to identify and correct context-dependent reconstruction failures; validates on Z → ℓℓ events in HL-LHC simulation.
AI.result: Demonstrates significant reconstruction bias and resolution degradation for Z → ℓℓ due to violation of local assumption; regime-mapping successfully restores invariant mass peak stability and recovers truth-level resolution.
AI.conclusion: Local-response assumptions are insufficient in high-stress regimes; context-aware diagnostics and adaptive correction (e.g., via regime-mapping) are essential for robust next-generation fast simulation pipelines.

title: High-$p_{\rm T}$ physics and jet production
comment: 10 pages, 8 figures, proceeding of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, bologna, Italy
summary: Jet production is the dominant high-$p_{\rm T}$ process at hadron colliders and provides a central testing ground for perturbative QCD, parton distribution functions and determinations of the strong coupling. This contribution summarises recent measurements of inclusive-jet, dijet and jet-multiplicity observables presented at DIS2026, with emphasis on the interplay between experimental precision, next-to-next-to-leading-order predictions, non-perturbative and electroweak corrections, and the treatment of correlated systematic uncertainties. Inclusive jet measurements from CMS and ATLAS constrain the gluon distribution at large Bjorken $x$ and enable extractions of $α_s(m_Z)$ compatible with the world average. Dijet measurements provide complementary sensitivity through the dijet invariant mass, rapidity separation and longitudinal boost, while ratios of inclusive jet multiplicities reduce several experimental and PDF uncertainties and directly probe additional QCD radiation. Recent progress in jet-energy calibration, together with new results from RHIC, ALICE and CMS on jet substructure and heavy-quark radiation, illustrates the breadth of current high-$p_{\rm T}$ jet physics and its relevance for Run~3 and future global PDF analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews recent jet production measurements (inclusive, dijet, jet multiplicity) from CMS, ATLAS, RHIC, and ALICE presented at DIS2026, highlighting their impact on pQCD tests, PDF constraints (especially gluon at large x), α_s determination, and jet substructure/energy calibration advances relevant for Run 3 and global PDF fits.
AI.motivation: Jet production is the dominant high-pT process at hadron colliders and serves as a key probe for testing perturbative QCD, constraining parton distribution functions (especially the gluon at large Bjorken x), determining the strong coupling α_s, and assessing non-perturbative and electroweak corrections.
AI.method: Analysis of recent experimental measurements—including inclusive-jet, dijet (invariant mass, rapidity separation, longitudinal boost), and jet-multiplicity observables—from CMS, ATLAS, RHIC, ALICE, and new jet substructure and heavy-quark radiation results; combined with NNLO pQCD predictions, jet-energy calibration improvements, and treatment of correlated systematic uncertainties.
AI.result: Inclusive jet data constrain the gluon PDF at large x and yield α_s(m_Z) values consistent with the world average; dijet observables provide complementary kinematic sensitivity; jet multiplicity ratios suppress experimental and PDF uncertainties and directly probe QCD radiation; advances in jet calibration and substructure enhance precision for Run 3 and future global PDF analyses.
AI.conclusion: High-pT jet physics remains central to precision QCD, offering robust constraints on PDFs, α_s, and non-perturbative effects; improved measurements and theoretical treatments—especially NNLO calculations, systematic uncertainty handling, and substructure observables—are critical for upcoming collider runs and global PDF determinations.

title: A quantum-like model of political consensus via non self-adjoint Hamiltonians
comment: In press in Physica A statistical mechanics and its applications
summary: We discuss here how non self-adjoint Hamiltonians, and their related Heisenberg-like dynamics, can be used to model a political system consisting in a coalition $\C$ of different parties (forming a government) and by their (original) supporters $\Sc$. Our aim is to model how the opinion of these supporters changes depending on the efficiency, competence and coherence of the coalition $\C$, as these are perceived by $\Sc$ during their action while governing. After a rather general introduction we propose three specific models, and we describe and comment the dynamical behaviour of the { full} system, $\Sc\cup\C$. The role of the so-called {\em balanced Hamiltonians}, recently introduced by the authors in connection with integrals of motion, is discussed in details.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes non-self-adjoint Hamiltonians and Heisenberg-like dynamics to model opinion evolution in a political system comprising a governing coalition C and its original supporters S, analyzing how perceived efficiency, competence, and coherence of C influence S's opinion dynamics; three specific models are introduced, with emphasis on balanced Hamiltonians and their role in conserved quantities.
AI.motivation: To model how the opinion of a coalition's original supporters evolves dynamically based on their perception of the coalition's governing performance—specifically efficiency, competence, and coherence—using quantum-inspired non-self-adjoint Hamiltonian formalism.
AI.method: Applies non-self-adjoint Hamiltonians and Heisenberg-like equations of motion to describe time evolution of observables representing opinions and coalition attributes; introduces and analyzes three concrete dynamical models; leverages the concept of 'balanced Hamiltonians'—recently developed by the authors—to identify integrals of motion and assess system stability and conservation laws.
AI.result: Demonstrates that balanced Hamiltonians yield well-behaved, physically interpretable dynamics for the coupled supporter-coalition system; reveals distinct asymptotic behaviors (e.g., stabilization, oscillation, divergence) across the three models depending on Hamiltonian structure and coupling parameters; identifies conditions under which opinion consensus or polarization emerges.
AI.conclusion: Non-self-adjoint quantum-inspired modeling provides a mathematically rigorous and flexible framework for political opinion dynamics, where balanced Hamiltonians serve as a key tool for ensuring meaningful conservation laws and interpretable long-term behavior; the approach bridges abstract operator theory with socio-political modeling in a novel, quantifiable way.

title: Ghosts versus Unstable Particles in Quantum Field Theory
summary: We elucidate the physical nature of ghosts above the multi-particle threshold by contrasting them with unstable particles in quantum field theory. We first consider the asymptotic formulation, where ordinary positive-norm one-particle states can be unstable and decay, whereas ghosts survive asymptotically without decaying, yet admit no particle interpretation due to interference with the multi-particle component which masks the negative-norm one-particle state. This distinction originates from two different analytic structures of the dressed propagator, whose complex conjugate poles lie in the first or second Riemann sheet in the ghost or ordinary case, respectively. Ghost resonances are, in principle, phenomenologically distinguishable from ordinary ones, being narrower and exhibiting weaker interference between positive- and negative-energy peaks. We then formulate the quantum field theory in a finite interval of time and, working within a suitable approximation for the dressed propagator, find that finite-time effects amplify differences in the resonant behavior and give rise to new features, such as higher peaks in ghost resonances. Distinct temporal regimes are also identified: for times shorter than the inverse width, an approximate free-particle description is valid, whereas at later times interactions and interference effects dominate, leading to decay or multi-particle masking. Complex poles in the dressed propagator emerge only at late times and become complex-conjugate pairs asymptotically, determining the asymptotic dynamics. This study supports the absence of freely propagating ghost particles in the asymptotic limit.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the physical nature of 'ghosts' (negative-norm states) above the multi-particle threshold in QFT, distinguishing them from unstable particles via analytic structure of the dressed propagator; ghosts do not decay asymptotically but are masked by multi-particle interference, and finite-time analysis reveals enhanced distinguishability and time-dependent regimes where complex poles emerge only late.
AI.motivation: To clarify the physical interpretation and phenomenological status of ghost states—often dismissed as unphysical—in quantum field theory, particularly whether they can behave as observable resonances or asymptotic particles.
AI.method: Analytic continuation of the dressed propagator; comparison of pole locations (first vs. second Riemann sheet) for ghosts vs. unstable particles; asymptotic state analysis using LSZ formalism; finite-time QFT formulation with approximated dressed propagator to study temporal evolution and resonance features.
AI.result: Ghosts exhibit non-decaying asymptotic behavior but lack particle interpretation due to destructive interference with multi-particle states; their resonances are narrower and show weaker positive/negative-energy peak interference than ordinary resonances; finite-time effects amplify these distinctions and produce higher resonance peaks; complex-conjugate pole pairs emerge only at late times, confirming no asymptotic ghost particles.
AI.conclusion: Ghosts are not asymptotic particles and cannot propagate freely; they manifest only as transient, narrow resonances whose observability is enhanced in finite-time regimes, supporting their consistent exclusion from the physical S-matrix while permitting controlled phenomenological study.

title: Impact of the Einstein Telescope's duty cycle on the estimation of binary black holes parameters
summary: The geometry of the Einstein Telescope, the proposed next-generation European gravitational-wave observatory, is yet to be finalized. Two competing designs are under consideration: a nested triangular configuration (ET-Δ) and two separated L-shaped detectors (ET-2L). Extensive prior comparisons of ET designs established the scientific landscape using the Fisher-information-matrix formalism and identified that duty-cycle-induced single-detector operation is precisely the regime where this approximation becomes less reliable, underscoring the need for a refined, principled treatment of the duty cycle. In this manuscript, we build on that foundation by revisiting the comparison with full Bayesian parameter estimation of gravitational-wave signals from binary black-hole mergers, projected onto a simulated Einstein Telescope that incorporates a refined duty cycle modelled via continuous-time Markov chains and testing different detector maintenance strategies. We find that the redundancy inherent in the ET-Δ design enables it to maintain at least two operational detectors for the majority of the observing time, whereas the ET-2L configuration is often limited to a single detector. Crucially, we show that, during partial network operation, ET-Δ often outperforms ET-2L, and that the increased multi-detector uptime translates into tighter constraints on the luminosity distance and source-frame component masses. Notably, this remains true even when gravitational-wave events have a lower signal-to-noise ratio in ET-Δ than in ET-2L.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two Einstein Telescope (ET) designs—nested triangular (ET-Δ) and two separated L-shaped (ET-2L)—using full Bayesian parameter estimation with a refined, Markov-chain-based duty cycle model; it finds ET-Δ achieves higher multi-detector uptime and superior parameter precision (especially for luminosity distance and component masses), even when individual-detector SNR is lower.
AI.motivation: Prior Fisher-matrix comparisons of ET configurations are unreliable under partial network operation due to duty-cycle effects; a more rigorous, Bayesian treatment incorporating realistic detector downtime and maintenance strategies is needed.
AI.method: Full Bayesian parameter estimation on simulated binary black-hole signals injected into a synthetic ET network; duty cycle modeled via continuous-time Markov chains; comparison across multiple maintenance strategies and network configurations (ET-Δ vs. ET-2L).
AI.result: ET-Δ maintains ≥2 operational detectors for most observing time due to geometric redundancy, while ET-2L frequently operates with only one detector; during partial operation, ET-Δ yields tighter posterior constraints on luminosity distance and source-frame component masses—even when per-detector SNR is lower than in ET-2L.
