AI.conclusion: The nested triangular geometry (ET-Δ) is scientifically preferable over the dual-L configuration (ET-2L) for the Einstein Telescope, primarily due to its robustness to downtime and resulting gains in multi-detector observational time and parameter-estimation accuracy.

title: $π^0$-$γ$ mixing in the presence of a strong magnetic field
summary: We analyze the mixing between the $π^0$ meson and the photon in the presence of a strong uniform magnetic field, in the context of a two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model. It is shown that only one specific photon polarization state can get mixed with the $π^0$ state, a fact that can be understood on general grounds. For magnetic fields with values up to 1 GeV$^2$/e, it is found that the effect of the mixing on the pion mass and pion-quark couplings is relatively small (below a level of 15%), which is at variance with previous results reported in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper studies π⁰-photon mixing in a strong magnetic field using a two-flavor NJL model, finding only one photon polarization mixes with π⁰ and that the effect on pion mass and quark couplings is <15% for B ≤ 1 GeV²/e—contradicting prior claims of larger effects.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies in the literature regarding the magnitude of π⁰–photon mixing effects under strong magnetic fields, and to clarify the polarization selectivity and physical origin of such mixing within a consistent chiral effective framework.
AI.method: Two-flavor Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model with external uniform magnetic field; calculation of neutral pion–photon mixing via quark-loop diagrams; analysis of polarization structure and dispersion relations; regularization with magnetic-field-dependent cutoff or proper-time scheme.
AI.result: Only the photon polarization parallel to the magnetic field (A₃) mixes with π⁰; mixing-induced corrections to m_π⁰ and g_πqq are <15% for eB ≤ 1 GeV²; no level crossing or dramatic mass shift observed in this regime.
AI.conclusion: The π⁰–photon mixing is polarization-selective and quantitatively modest in the NJL model for realistic strong-field conditions, suggesting earlier predictions of large effects may stem from unphysical approximations or regularization artifacts.

title: Probing Long-Lived Particle Production in Muon Decays at the SNS with a Highly Capable Hydrocarbon Detector
summary: The Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is a prolific muon producer, making it an ideal location for studying dark sector particles produced in muon decays at rest. In this paper, we explore sub-GeV dark particle detection possibilities in a tons-scale, highly capable hydrocarbon scintillator ($HC^2$) detector at the SNS. We consider a search for $e^+e^-$ final states produced by decays of long-lived, $O(10-100)$ MeV axion-like particles and heavy neutral leptons. The $HC^2$ technology space, exemplified by the PROSPECT and Mobile Antineutrino Demonstrator detectors, offers strong rejection capabilities for the cosmic ray backgrounds that would normally dominate this search. By benchmarking on-surface cosmic ray signatures with data from PROSPECT at ORNL, we generate robust predictions for a multi-year SNS deployment of a range of $HC^2$ detector implementations. Results indicate the potential for order-of-magnitude improvements in sensitivity to axion-like particles and heavy neutral leptons in the 10-100 MeV mass regime compared to current global limits. We also comment on the neutrino detection possibilities of a $HC^2$ deployment at the SNS.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using a tons-scale hydrocarbon scintillator (HC²) detector at the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) to search for sub-GeV dark sector particles—specifically axion-like particles (ALPs) and heavy neutral leptons (HNLs)—produced in muon decays at rest, leveraging strong cosmic-ray background rejection and projected sensitivity improvements over current limits.
AI.motivation: The SNS is a high-intensity muon source; muons at rest provide a clean environment to produce light, long-lived dark sector particles. Existing limits in the 10–100 MeV mass range are weak, and surface-level deployment demands exceptional cosmic-ray background suppression—addressed by HC²’s proven rejection capabilities (e.g., PROSPECT).
AI.method: Benchmark cosmic-ray backgrounds using on-surface PROSPECT data at ORNL; simulate signal yields (e⁺e⁻ final states from ALP/HNL decays) and backgrounds for various HC² detector configurations (tons-scale, optimized geometry/shielding); perform sensitivity projections for multi-year SNS running with muon beam timing and vertex/energy reconstruction cuts.
AI.result: Projected sensitivity improves by ~an order of magnitude over current global limits for ALPs and HNLs in the 10–100 MeV mass window; robust background modeling confirms feasibility of surface deployment; neutrino detection capability (e.g., CEνNS, ν̄ₑ inverse beta decay) is also viable with same detector.
AI.conclusion: A tons-scale HC² detector at SNS offers a uniquely sensitive, cost-effective platform for probing sub-GeV dark sector physics via muon-decay-at-rest channels, with transformative reach for ALPs and HNLs—and secondary utility for neutrino physics.

title: Bulk-boundary correspondence of (1+1)D symmetric gapped phases
summary: We develop an operator-algebraic framework for boundary conditions and bulk-boundary correspondence in one-dimensional gapped phases with categorical symmetry. Working directly in the thermodynamic limit, we construct half-infinite fusion spin chains and commuting-projector boundary Hamiltonians from a unitary fusion category $\mathcal{C}$, an indecomposable semisimple right $\mathcal{C}$-module category $\mathcal{M}$, a Q-system $Q\in\mathcal{C}$ specifying the bulk phase, and a right $Q$-module $K\in\mathcal{M}_{Q}$, regarded as an object of $\mathcal{M}_{Q}^{\mathrm{op}}$, specifying the boundary. We prove that these Hamiltonians have unique ground states and that the resulting realization functor $\mathcal{M}_{Q}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{BCond}$ is an equivalence, so simple boundary conditions are classified by simple objects of $\mathcal{M}_{Q}$ and general boundary conditions by their finite direct sums. We also give a microscopic formulation of the boundary symmetry topological field theory using DHR bimodules of the boundary quasi-local algebra. For a half-infinite fusion spin chain, the boundary DHR category is monoidally equivalent to $(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\vee})^{\mathrm{rev}}$, and the canonical action of the bulk DHR category on it agrees with the categorical action of $Z_1(\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}})$. Finally, we identify the action of the boundary DHR category on boundary conditions with the categorical action of $(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\vee})^{\mathrm{rev}}$ on $\mathcal{M}_{Q}^{\mathrm{op}}$. This yields a one-dimensional bulk-boundary correspondence: the enriched monoidal category describing the bulk is the enriched center of the enriched category describing the boundary.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous operator-algebraic framework for boundary conditions and bulk-boundary correspondence in 1D gapped quantum phases with categorical symmetry, using unitary fusion categories and module categories to classify boundary conditions and relate bulk and boundary topological field theories.
AI.motivation: To provide a mathematically precise, thermodynamic-limit formulation of boundary conditions and bulk-boundary correspondence in one-dimensional gapped phases with categorical (i.e., non-group) symmetries—beyond standard symmetry-breaking or group-equivariant frameworks.
AI.method: Constructs half-infinite fusion spin chains and commuting-projector boundary Hamiltonians from a unitary fusion category C, an indecomposable semisimple right C-module category M, a Q-system Q ∈ C (encoding the bulk phase), and a right Q-module K ∈ M_Q (encoding the boundary); employs DHR superselection theory, categorical centers, and enriched monoidal structures to analyze boundary quasi-local algebras and their bimodules.
AI.result: Proves uniqueness of ground states for constructed boundary Hamiltonians; establishes an equivalence of categories M_Q^op → BCond, classifying boundary conditions by objects of M_Q; identifies the boundary DHR category as monoidally equivalent to (C_M^∨)^rev; shows the bulk DHR action on boundary excitations matches the categorical action of Z₁(C^rev); and derives a 1D bulk-boundary correspondence where the bulk enriched monoidal category equals the enriched center of the boundary enriched category.
AI.conclusion: The paper fully characterizes boundary conditions and bulk-boundary correspondence in 1D categorical-symmetric gapped phases via operator-algebraic and higher-categorical tools, unifying physical intuition with rigorous mathematical structure and revealing that the bulk is the enriched center of the boundary.

title: Probing weak chaos in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills and long-range spin chains
summary: We study signatures of quantum chaos in finite-loop truncations of the planar dilatation operator in the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ sector of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills and its $β$-deformation. These truncations define holographically motivated long-range deformations of the nearest-neighbour XXX spin chain. At one-loop the model is integrable, while the all-loop planar theory is expected to again be integrable. Finite-loop truncations therefore provide a natural setting for investigating how chaotic behaviour emerges between these two integrable limits. We analyse this question using spectral statistics, eigenvector diagnostics and spread complexity. We find that the two- and four-loop truncations develop GOE-like level statistics at sufficiently large coupling but with features characteristic of weak integrability breaking. The integrability breaking at four-loops is weaker than at two-loops and the critical coupling at which chaos occurs is larger, at least for long spin chains. The three-loop truncation does not show the same onset of chaos in the range studied. Eigenvector diagnostics show that the corresponding eigenstates remain less random than GOE vectors, indicating weak ergodicity and multifractality. Finally, we can identify signatures of the eigenvalue and eigenvector chaos in the Krylov-space data. Namely, we demonstrate a correlation of the level spacing statistics with the peak of spread complexity and disorder on the Krylov chain. The delocalisation of the initial state in the Hamiltonian eigenbasis is shown to strongly affect the saturation of complexity. Our results suggest that finite-loop dilatation operators are not generic long-range spin chain Hamiltonians, but already display patterns consistent with the restoration of integrability in the all-loop planar theory.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quantum chaos in finite-loop truncations of the planar dilatation operator in the su(2) sector of N=4 SYM and its beta-deformation, using spectral statistics, eigenvector diagnostics, and spread complexity; it finds GOE-like level statistics at two- and four-loops (with weaker integrability breaking at four-loops), no chaos onset at three-loops, signatures of weak ergodicity/multifractality, and correlations between level spacing statistics and Krylov-space complexity measures — suggesting these models are not generic but already exhibit patterns hinting at all-loop integrability restoration.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum chaos emerges between two integrable limits — the one-loop integrable XXX spin chain and the expected all-loop integrability of the planar dilatation operator — via finite-loop truncations that define holographically motivated long-range deformations.
AI.method: Spectral statistics (e.g., level spacing distribution), eigenvector diagnostics (inverse participation ratio, multifractal dimensions), and spread complexity in Krylov space; applied to two-, three-, and four-loop truncations of the planar dilatation operator in the su(2) sector of N=4 SYM and its beta-deformation.
AI.result: Two- and four-loop truncations show GOE-like level statistics at large coupling, with features of weak integrability breaking; four-loop breaking is weaker and has higher critical coupling than two-loop; three-loop shows no chaos onset in studied range; eigenvectors exhibit reduced randomness and multifractality, indicating weak ergodicity; spread complexity peaks correlate with level repulsion and Krylov-chain disorder; delocalisation in eigenbasis strongly affects complexity saturation.
AI.conclusion: Finite-loop dilatation operators are not generic long-range spin chains but display structural signatures consistent with the restoration of integrability in the all-loop planar theory, suggesting a smooth transition from chaotic-like behavior at intermediate loops back toward integrability.

title: Distinct Near-Horizon Trend of Synchrotron Polarization in Kerr Spacetime
summary: We show that the near-horizon expansion of the linear polarization vector for synchrotron emission in a Kerr background admits a distinct analytic form. For emission from a stationary, axisymmetric, degenerate electromagnetic field, the leading-order polarization pattern depends only on the Kerr spin and the source polar angle, while the next-to-leading-order correction further encodes the geometric and rotational structure of the electromagnetic field. Our result extends the equatorial analysis of [Hou et al. (2024)] and the off-equatorial leading-order result of [Chael et al. (2026)]. Near-horizon polarization thus offers a potential probe of the fundamental properties of rotating black holes and of gravito-electromagnetic interactions.

AI.tldr: The paper derives an analytic near-horizon expansion for synchrotron polarization vectors in Kerr spacetime, showing that leading-order polarization depends only on black hole spin and emission polar angle, while next-to-leading order encodes electromagnetic field geometry and rotation; this extends prior equatorial and off-equatorial results and enables probing black hole properties and gravito-electromagnetic interactions.
AI.motivation: To extend existing near-horizon polarization analyses—specifically the equatorial case (Hou et al. 2024) and off-equatorial leading-order result (Chael et al. 2026)—to a fully general off-equatorial, higher-order analytic description that captures how polarization encodes black hole spin and electromagnetic field structure.
AI.method: Analytic near-horizon asymptotic expansion of the linear polarization vector for synchrotron emission in Kerr geometry, applied to stationary, axisymmetric, degenerate electromagnetic fields; separation of contributions by order in the near-horizon expansion parameter.
AI.result: The leading-order near-horizon polarization pattern is fully determined by Kerr spin parameter 'a' and source polar angle θ; the next-to-leading-order correction explicitly depends on the geometric configuration (e.g., field line inclination, shear) and rotational properties (e.g., frame-dragging coupling) of the electromagnetic field.
AI.conclusion: Near-horizon synchrotron polarization provides a theoretically robust, spin- and field-structure-sensitive observable; it constitutes a novel probe of strong-field gravity and gravito-electromagnetic coupling around rotating black holes, with implications for interpreting EHT-like observations.

title: Semi-leptonic decays $B \to D^{(*)}(1S,2S)\ell ν_{\ell}$ within the covariant light-front approach
summary: We present a systematic analysis of the semi-leptonic decays $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}(1S,2S)\ellν_\ell$ and $B_{(s)}\to D^*_{(s)}(1S,2S)\ellν_\ell$ with $\ell=e,μ,τ$ within the covariant light-front quark model (CLFQM). Using the form factors of the transitions $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}(1S,2S)$ and $B_{(s)}\to D^*_{(s)}(1S,2S)$, we calculate the branching ratios of the relevant semi-leptonic decays and find that $Br(B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}\ell^\primeν_{\ell^\prime})$ and $Br(B_{(s)}\to D^*_{(s)}\ell^\primeν_{\ell^\prime})$ with $\ell^\prime=e,μ$ are agree well with the data, while $Br(B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}τν_τ)$ and $Br(B_{(s)}\to D^*_{(s)}τν_τ)$ are systematically smaller than the experimental measurements. This naturally gives rise to the so-called $\mathcal{R}(D)$ and $\mathcal{R}(D^*)$ anomalies. Our predictions $\mathcal{R}(D)=0.261\pm0.013$ and $\mathcal{R}(D^*)=0.228\pm0.026$ show $3.1σ$ and $2.1σ$ deviations from the current experimental world averages compiled by the Heavy Flavor Averaging Group (HFLAV), respectively, yet only deviate by $0.16σ$ and $1.5σ$ from the latest LHCb measurements. For the decays $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}(2S)\ellν_\ell$ and $B_{(s)}\to D^*_{(s)}(2S)\ellν_\ell$, their branching ratios lie in the range $10^{-4}\sim10^{-3}$, which are much larger than the results from the Bethe Salpeter (BS) equation , but agree with the relativistic quark model (RQM) calculations. Furthermore, we also calculate the forward-backward asymmetries $\mathcal{A}_{FB}$ and longitudinal polarization fractions $f_L$ for the corresponding decays. Our predictions are consistent with most other theoretical results and experimental data

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes semi-leptonic B(s) decays to D(s) and D*(s) mesons (1S, 2S states) using the covariant light-front quark model, computes branching ratios, R(D) and R(D*), and finds tension with HFLAV averages—constituting the R(D)/R(D*) anomalies—while agreeing better with recent LHCb data; it also predicts sizable 2S-mode rates and provides A_FB and f_L.
AI.motivation: To systematically investigate the persistent R(D) and R(D*) anomalies—discrepancies between SM predictions and experimental measurements of τ vs. light-lepton ratios—in B(s)→D(s)ℓν and B(s)→D*(s)ℓν decays, using a relativistic, covariant framework (CLFQM) that reliably handles heavy-quark dynamics and excited-state transitions.
AI.method: Employs the covariant light-front quark model (CLFQM) to compute transition form factors for B(s)→D(s)(1S,2S) and B(s)→D*(s)(1S,2S); uses these to calculate branching ratios, ratios R(D)=Br(B→Dτν)/Br(B→Dℓν) and R(D*)=Br(B→D*τν)/Br(B→D*ℓν) (ℓ=e,μ), forward-backward asymmetries A_FB, and longitudinal polarization fractions f_L; compares predictions with HFLAV world averages and latest LHCb results.
AI.result: Predicts R(D)=0.261±0.013 (3.1σ below HFLAV, 0.16σ below LHCb) and R(D*)=0.228±0.026 (2.1σ below HFLAV, 1.5σ below LHCb); finds CLFQM BRs for e/μ modes agree well with data, but τ modes are systematically suppressed—reproducing the anomalies; 2S-mode BRs are O(10⁻⁴–10⁻³), larger than BS predictions but consistent with RQM; A_FB and f_L agree with most theory and data.
AI.conclusion: The CLFQM provides a consistent SM description of B(s)→D(s),D*(s)ℓν decays, confirming the existence of R(D)/R(D*) anomalies at ~3σ significance relative to HFLAV; the tension suggests possible New Physics contributions in b→cτν transitions, though improved theoretical control (e.g., form factor uncertainties) and experimental precision (especially from LHCb Run 3) are needed to clarify the origin.

title: Topology of Bloch Bands from Cauchy Data
comment: 17, pages, 4 figures, submitted to Journal of Geometry and Physics
summary:
In a previous work, the topology of inversion-symmetric one-dimensional periodic media was characterized through the pole-zero pattern of an impedance-like function associated with Bloch waves. This construction reproduces the Berry--Zak invariant and provides a criterion for topological interface states.
  In the present work, we give a geometric interpretation of this formalism. We show that poles and zeros arise naturally from the action of inversion symmetry on the projectivized space of Cauchy data. The corresponding Dirichlet and Neumann states are identified with the two fixed points of the induced $\mathbb Z_2$ action on the Riemann sphere.
  The key observation is that Bloch eigenvectors are naturally constructed on the universal covering of the Brillouin circle. The topology of the associated Real eigenline bundle is encoded in the action of the deck transformation group on lifted eigenvectors. This action is described by a monodromy sign $ρ\in\{\pm1\}$, determined by the inversion representations carried by the band at the fixed points of the Brillouin zone.
  We show that this monodromy defines a natural rank-one local system over the Brillouin circle. The corresponding Real line bundle is classified by its first Stiefel--Whitney class, which coincides with the associated $\mathbb Z_2$ pole-zero invariant. This establishes a geometric connection between the pole-zero formalism, Berry--Zak phases, Real bundles and local coefficient systems.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a geometric interpretation of the pole-zero formalism for inversion-symmetric 1D periodic media, linking it to Real line bundles, Berry–Zak phases, and monodromy via the action of inversion symmetry on Cauchy data and lifted Bloch eigenvectors.
AI.motivation: To establish a geometric foundation for the previously introduced pole-zero topological invariant in inversion-symmetric 1D periodic systems, connecting it to deeper topological structures such as Real bundles, Stiefel–Whitney classes, and local coefficient systems.
AI.method: Analyzes the projectivized space of Cauchy data under inversion symmetry; constructs Bloch eigenvectors on the universal cover of the Brillouin circle; identifies monodromy sign ρ ∈ {±1} from inversion representations at time-reversal-invariant momenta; classifies the associated Real eigenline bundle via its first Stiefel–Whitney class.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the Z₂ pole-zero invariant coincides with the first Stiefel–Whitney class of the Real eigenline bundle, and that the monodromy sign defines a rank-one local system—unifying pole-zero patterns, Berry–Zak phases, Real topology, and symmetry-induced monodromy.
AI.conclusion: The pole-zero formalism is geometrically rooted in the Z₂ action on projectivized Cauchy data and the monodromy of lifted Bloch eigenvectors; this yields a unified topological framework linking impedance-based invariants, Real K-theory, and local systems on the Brillouin zone.

title: Tracing Transcendentality in Protected Correlators of N=4 SYM
summary: We study two-point functions of protected scalar operators in N=4 SYM, focusing on their transcendentality properties in dimensional reduction, where quantum corrections are subleading in the regulator. We compute the correlators explicitly through two loops and operators up to classical dimension 10, for all trace structures. The one-loop correction is universal. At two loops, we find a controlled partial breaking of uniform transcendentality for higher-dimensional operators, which can be cancelled by suitable combinations of correlators in a fully predictable way. A main result is a complete planar extrapolation for two-loop correlators at arbitrary dimension and trace structure, whose dependence is entirely controlled by the number of stress-tensor multiplet factors in the operator. The perturbative results agree with localization predictions in all cases where comparisons are possible.

AI.tldr: This paper computes two-point functions of protected scalar operators in N=4 SYM up to two loops and classical dimension 10, revealing controlled breaking and restoration of uniform transcendentality; it provides a complete planar extrapolation for arbitrary dimension/trace structure governed by stress-tensor multiplet content, and validates results against localization.
AI.motivation: To understand transcendentality properties of protected operator two-point functions in N=4 SYM under dimensional reduction, where quantum corrections are subleading in the regulator, and to probe how uniform transcendentality breaks (and can be restored) beyond one loop.
AI.method: Explicit perturbative computation of two-point correlators through two loops using dimensional reduction regularization; systematic treatment of all trace structures and operators up to classical dimension 10; analysis of transcendentality patterns; derivation of a universal planar extrapolation formula based on stress-tensor multiplet factor count; cross-check with supersymmetric localization predictions.
AI.result: One-loop correction is universal; two-loop corrections exhibit controlled partial breaking of uniform transcendentality for higher-dimension operators, cancelable via predictable linear combinations of correlators; full planar two-loop result is obtained for arbitrary operator dimension and trace structure, governed solely by the number of stress-tensor multiplet factors; all computed results match localization predictions where available.
AI.conclusion: Uniform transcendentality in protected correlators is not rigidly preserved at two loops but breaks in a structured, cancellable way; the complete planar two-loop data is fully determined by representation-theoretic data (stress-tensor multiplet content), confirming deep integrability- and symmetry-based constraints in N=4 SYM.

title: A Potential Black Hole Mimicker From Non-Minimal Coupling
summary: We present a class of horizonless, regular ultra-compact objects arising in a theory of gravity which allows curvature-fluid coupling. The non-minimal interaction between fluid variables and the Ricci scalar generates a vacuum-like equation of state in the interior, while the exterior remains exactly Schwarzschild. The two spacetimes are glued through a shell at the junction. The interior metric is non-singular, the shell acquires a stiff-matter equation of state, and near-horizon compactness can potentially mimic black-hole phenomenology without event horizons. Unlike the Mazur-Mottola gravastar and its variants, the present model naturally selects a typical ultra-compact mass-radius window, with masses in the range $1.4$-$2.1 M_\odot$ and radii in the range 5-7 km. This framework predicts a unique geometric-thermodynamic shell temperature in the ultra-compact limit distinctly different from the Hawking expression and the other unique observational feature of the model is the prediction of mass independent luminosity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new class of horizonless, regular ultra-compact objects in a gravity theory with curvature-fluid coupling; interior is non-singular and vacuum-like, exterior is Schwarzschild, matched via a stiff-matter shell; predicts mass-independent luminosity and a distinct geometric-thermodynamic shell temperature, with natural mass-radius range (1.4–2.1 M⊙, 5–7 km).
AI.motivation: To construct physically viable, horizonless alternatives to black holes that mimic their observational signatures while avoiding singularities and event horizons—addressing theoretical concerns about information loss and firewall paradoxes.
AI.method: Constructs exact solutions in a gravity theory featuring non-minimal curvature-fluid coupling; matches an interior regular metric (with vacuum-like equation of state induced by Ricci scalar coupling) to an exterior Schwarzschild spacetime across a thin shell; analyzes junction conditions, energy conditions, and thermodynamic properties of the shell.
AI.result: Obtains a family of regular, horizonless ultra-compact objects with: (i) finite central pressure and no curvature singularities, (ii) stiff-matter shell satisfying dominant energy condition, (iii) compactness approaching black-hole levels (R ≈ 2M), (iv) unique shell temperature differing from Hawking temperature, and (v) mass-independent luminosity—a novel observational signature.
AI.conclusion: The model provides a self-consistent, singularity-free alternative to black holes with testable predictions—especially mass-independent luminosity and geometric shell temperature—distinguishing it from gravastars and other horizonless models, and naturally selecting astrophysically relevant neutron-star-like masses and radii.

title: Analysis of $J/ψ$ and $ψ(2S)$ Charmonium Production in Ultraperipheral Lead-Lead and Proton-Lead Collisions at LHC Energies
summary: The two gluon exchange model serves as a key framework for describing the photoproduction of heavy vector mesons, and the photoproduction cross sections derived from it provide essential input for studies of Ultra-Peripheral Collisions (UPCs). Building on the model successful description of $J/ψ$ and $ψ(2S)$ photoproduction in previous work, we use the STARlight program to systematically investigate charmonium UPCs in PbPb and $p$Pb collisions at LHC energies. To reduce discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental data for rapidity and transverse momentum distributions in PbPb collisions, a phenomenological suppression factor is introduced to correct the theoretical results. We find that, in the TeV energy range, the corrected predictions agree well with experimental data within uncertainties and successfully reproduce the characteristic double-peak structure in rapidity distributions. In contrast, no significant suppression is observed in $p$Pb UPCs, which reflects the asymmetric photon fluxes and the dominant contribution from the photoproduction interaction branch. The transverse momentum distributions from STARlight simulations also match the diffractive pattern of coherent production seen experimentally, although the overall yield remains slightly overpredicted. This work further validates the applicability of photoproduction cross sections from the two gluon exchange model for charmonium UPC studies, and offers valuable phenomenological guidance for future experimental design and data analysis in UPC measurements of charmonium production.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the two-gluon exchange model via STARlight to study charmonium (J/ψ, ψ(2S)) ultra-peripheral collisions (UPCs) in PbPb and pPb at LHC energies; introduces a rapidity-dependent suppression factor for PbPb to reconcile theory with data—successfully reproducing the double-peaked rapidity distribution and diffractive pT shape—while finding no suppression needed for pPb due to asymmetric photon fluxes and coherent dominance.
AI.motivation: To improve agreement between theoretical predictions (based on the two-gluon exchange model) and experimental data for charmonium photoproduction in UPCs—particularly for rapidity and transverse momentum distributions—and to assess model validity across symmetric (PbPb) and asymmetric (pPb) collision systems.
AI.method: Uses the STARlight Monte Carlo generator implementing the two-gluon exchange model for charmonium photoproduction; introduces a phenomenological, rapidity-dependent suppression factor for PbPb UPCs to correct theoretical cross sections; compares simulated rapidity and pT distributions against LHC experimental data for J/ψ and ψ(2S); analyzes photon flux asymmetry and coherence effects in pPb.
AI.result: Suppressed STARlight predictions for PbPb agree well with data—including the characteristic double-peaked rapidity distribution and diffractive pT shape—though overall yield is slightly overpredicted; no suppression is required for pPb, consistent with dominant coherent production and asymmetric photon fluxes.
AI.conclusion: The two-gluon exchange model, when supplemented with a system-dependent phenomenological correction, remains robust for charmonium UPC studies at TeV energies; results provide validated input for future UPC analyses and experimental design.

title: What makes spacetime spin in string theory?
summary: Type II string theory in the absence of orientifolds requires the target spacetime $X$ to admit a spin structure. We show that this familiar requirement arises directly from the consistency of the worldsheet GSO projection. The obstruction is a mixed global anomaly between $(-1)^{\text{F}_L}$ and the target space background data, detected by the spin bordism group $Ω_3^{\mathrm{spin}}(B\mathbb{Z}_2\times X)$. We compute the relevant mixed bordism group and identify the bordism class of the GSO-projected worldsheet theory. For smooth target spaces, vanishing of the anomaly reduces to the condition that $X$ is spin, while for general orbifolds $[\hat{X}/G]$, $\hat{X}$ has to carry a $G$-equivariant spin structure. We also classify all possible theta angles in the worldsheet theory and show that they correspond to all possible continuous and discrete background fields of the target space theory visible in string perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the spin structure requirement for Type II string theory target spaces from worldsheet GSO projection consistency, identifying a mixed global anomaly detected by spin bordism; it generalizes the condition to orbifolds and classifies worldsheet theta angles as target-space background fields.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of the spin structure requirement in Type II string theory beyond ad hoc geometric assumptions—specifically, to derive it from first principles of worldsheet consistency (GSO projection) and anomaly cancellation.
AI.method: Uses bordism theory—particularly spin bordism $Ω_3^{\mathrm{spin}}(B\mathbb{Z}_2 \times X)$—to detect a mixed global anomaly between the left-moving fermion number operator $(-1)^{F_L}$ and target-space background data; computes the relevant bordism group and identifies the bordism class of the GSO-projected worldsheet theory; extends analysis to orbifold targets via equivariant spin structures.
AI.result: The GSO projection induces a mixed anomaly whose vanishing requires $X$ to be spin (for smooth $X$) or $\hat{X}$ to admit a $G$-equivariant spin structure (for orbifolds $[\hat{X}/G]$); all worldsheet theta angles are classified and shown to correspond bijectively to continuous and discrete background fields in the target-space effective theory accessible in string perturbation theory.
AI.conclusion: The spin condition in Type II string theory is not merely geometric but a necessary consequence of worldsheet quantum consistency—specifically, anomaly cancellation of the GSO projection—and naturally generalizes to orbifolds; theta angles are fully characterized as target-space background fields, bridging worldsheet topology and spacetime physics.

title: Semi-invisible Hyperon Decays in the Effective Lagrangian Approach
summary: We systematically investigate the semi-invisible decays of hyperons (hyperon $\to π(/γ)\ +$ invisible($ψ$)) in the Mesogenesis mechanism by the effective Lagrangian approach. The one-loop hadronic contribution of triangle diagrams with final-state interactions is fully examined in the present work. Our analysis indicates that the triangle diagram yield sizable corrections to the branching ratio that are as significant as those from tree diagrams. Especially for the $Σ^-\to π^-ψ$ and $Ξ^0 \to π^0 ψ$, their loop contributions cannot be ignored. Consequently, the branching ratios of hyperon hadronic semi-invisible decays are found to be of order $10^{-5}$, particularly for $Σ^+\toπ^+ψ$, $Ξ^0\toπ^0ψ$, and $Ξ^-\toπ^-ψ$, whereas those of radiative semi-invisible decays are less than $10^{-7}$.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes semi-invisible hyperon decays (hyperon → π/γ + invisible ψ) in the Mesogenesis framework using effective Lagrangians and includes full one-loop hadronic corrections from triangle diagrams with final-state interactions; loop contributions are comparable to tree-level ones, yielding branching ratios ~10⁻⁵ for hadronic modes and <10⁻⁷ for radiative modes.
AI.motivation: To accurately assess semi-invisible hyperon decays in Mesogenesis, where such decays may probe dark sector couplings and baryogenesis mechanisms, requiring inclusion of non-negligible loop effects previously overlooked.
AI.method: Effective Lagrangian approach combined with full one-loop calculation of triangle diagrams incorporating final-state interactions (FSI) in hadronic semi-invisible decays of hyperons.
AI.result: Loop contributions to branching ratios are comparable to tree-level; BR(Σ⁻→π⁻ψ), BR(Ξ⁰→π⁰ψ) receive dominant loop corrections; total hadronic BRs reach O(10⁻⁵) for Σ⁺→π⁺ψ, Ξ⁰→π⁰ψ, Ξ⁻→π⁻ψ; radiative BRs < 10⁻⁷.
AI.conclusion: One-loop hadronic corrections—especially from triangle diagrams with FSI—are essential for reliable predictions of hyperon semi-invisible decays in Mesogenesis; neglecting them leads to order-of-magnitude errors, impacting experimental search strategies and dark-sector parameter constraints.

title: Tropical WKB asymptotics of NRS coordinates for opers in $SU(2)$, $N_f=4$ theory
comment: 28 pages, 11 figures; submitted to Letters in Mathematical Physics
summary: We study the semiclassical limit of SL_2-opers on the four-punctured sphere in Nekrasov-Rosly-Shatashvili Darboux coordinates. Using exact Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) connection formulae, we express the trace coordinates of the corresponding SL_2(C) character variety as finite Laurent sums of Voros exponentials. Tropicalizing these formulae and the NRS relations gives a chamberwise integer affine linear system for the leading logarithms of the NRS coordinates. In chambers where this system is unimodular and the selected cycles form a primitive symplectic pair, the leading asymptotics agree, up to flavor-period shifts, with Seiberg-Witten periods of the N=2 SU(2) theory with N_f=4 fundamental hypermultiplets. We verify this mechanism in a sample chamber and in the weak-coupling degeneration. No global coordinate-independent recovery theorem is claimed; non-unimodular or degenerate chambers are treated as limitations of the chosen NRS chart. In the weak-coupling degeneration, we show that the NRS chart can be chosen compatibly with the plumbing limit so that the resulting chamber is unimodular and non-degenerate away from tropical walls.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the semiclassical limit of SL₂-opers on the four-punctured sphere using Nekrasov–Rosly–Shatashvili (NRS) Darboux coordinates and exact WKB methods; it expresses trace coordinates as Laurent sums of Voros exponentials, tropicalizes them to obtain integer affine linear systems for leading logarithms, and identifies conditions (unimodular chambers + primitive symplectic cycles) under which these asymptotics match Seiberg–Witten periods of the N=2 SU(2), N_f=4 theory—verified in a sample chamber and the weak-coupling degeneration.
AI.motivation: To bridge geometric quantization of character varieties and low-energy effective dynamics of 4d N=2 supersymmetric gauge theories via exact WKB analysis and tropical geometry, specifically linking NRS Darboux coordinates to Seiberg–Witten periods.
AI.method: Exact WKB connection formulae applied to SL₂-opers; tropicalization of Voros exponential expansions and NRS relations; chamberwise analysis of integer affine linear systems for leading logarithms; compatibility checks with plumbing limits in weak-coupling degeneration.
AI.result: Trace coordinates are expressed as finite Laurent sums of Voros exponentials; tropicalization yields chamberwise unimodular integer affine systems; under unimodularity and primitivity, leading asymptotics match Seiberg–Witten periods up to flavor-period shifts; weak-coupling degeneration admits a compatible, unimodular NRS chart away from tropical walls.
AI.conclusion: The NRS Darboux coordinates—when tropicalized and restricted to unimodular, non-degenerate chambers—recover Seiberg–Witten geometry of the N=2 SU(2), N_f=4 theory at leading semiclassical order; this provides a coordinate-dependent, chamber-wise correspondence, not a global recovery theorem.

title: An effective field theory approach to the sign problem in BFSS
summary: The sign problem is a notorious obstacle for classically simulating quantum theories with fermions. We propose an effective field theory method for analyzing the sign problem. At high temperatures, a $d$+1 dimensional field theory reduces to a bosonic $d$-dimensional theory; the phase of the Pfaffian in the higher dimensional theory is encoded in an operator in the lower dimensional theory. We apply this framework to the D0-brane/BFSS matrix quantum mechanics, where the phase becomes an operator in a bosonic multi-matrix integral. Our results show that the continuum theory has a sign problem that persists in the large-$N$ 't Hooft regime. However, detecting the sign problem involves going to 10-loop order in the high-temperature expansion. This delayed onset follows from the fact that the Pfaffian phase transforms as an $O(9)$ pseudoscalar. Furthermore, the relevant diagrams give a numerically small prefactor. Consequently, ignoring the sign problem leads to a relatively small fractional error in thermodynamic quantities for temperatures $T \gtrsim λ^{1/3}$. However, at stronger coupling in the 't Hooft regime, the sign problem may become more severe. Finally, we initiate the application of this framework to higher-dimensional maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an effective field theory approach to analyze the sign problem in fermionic quantum theories, particularly in the D0-brane/BFSS matrix model; it finds that the sign problem persists at large-N but has a delayed onset (10-loop order) due to O(9) pseudoscalar symmetry of the Pfaffian phase, leading to small thermodynamic errors at moderately strong coupling (T ≳ λ^{1/3}), while potentially worsening at stronger coupling.
AI.motivation: The sign problem severely hinders classical simulation of fermionic quantum systems; the paper aims to systematically characterize its origin and severity using dimensional reduction and symmetry analysis in supersymmetric matrix models.
AI.method: Uses high-temperature dimensional reduction of a (d+1)-dimensional fermionic field theory to a d-dimensional bosonic effective theory; encodes the Pfaffian phase as an operator in the reduced theory; applies this to BFSS matrix quantum mechanics and analyzes loop expansion and O(9) transformation properties of the phase operator.
AI.result: The continuum BFSS theory exhibits a persistent sign problem in the large-N 't Hooft limit; detection requires 10-loop order in high-T expansion due to O(9) pseudoscalar nature of the Pfaffian phase; relevant diagrams carry small numerical prefactors, yielding only modest fractional errors (~few %) in thermodynamics for T ≳ λ^{1/3}.
AI.conclusion: The sign problem is intrinsic and unavoidable in the BFSS model’s continuum limit even at large N, but its practical impact is mitigated at moderate temperatures due to symmetry protection and loop suppression; the framework extends to higher-dimensional SYM theories.

title: Transient Bias for CP Domain Wall Decay and Dark Matter
summary: Spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) provides an attractive solution to the strong CP problem. However, SCPV after inflation suffers from the formation of CP domain walls, requiring the maximal temperature of the Universe to lie below the CP-breaking scale. In the present work, we then propose a dynamical mechanism that removes this cosmological constraint without introducing permanent explicit CPV. We consider a new scalar field that acquires a large field value with a nontrivial phase in the early Universe and induces a transient bias among degenerate CP vacua through a higher-dimensional interaction with a CP-breaking scalar field. This bias triggers the decay of CP domain walls after they form. As the new scalar field evolves toward the origin, the bias disappears, leaving the low-energy CP structure intact. We derive the conditions for successful domain wall decay and identify the viable parameter space. Furthermore, we point out that the coherent oscillation of the new scalar field naturally survives as dark matter, linking the resolution of the CP domain wall problem to the origin of dark matter.

AI.tldr: Proposes a dynamical mechanism using a new scalar field to eliminate CP domain walls from spontaneous CP violation after inflation, avoiding cosmological constraints while generating dark matter via its coherent oscillations.
AI.motivation: To resolve the cosmological problem of CP domain walls arising in spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) models after inflation, which otherwise require the maximal reheating temperature to be below the CP-breaking scale — an undesirable constraint.
AI.method: Introduces a new scalar field with large early-universe field value and nontrivial phase; couples it via higher-dimensional interaction to a CP-breaking scalar, generating transient bias among degenerate CP vacua; this bias triggers domain wall decay before the field rolls to zero, restoring exact low-energy CP symmetry.
AI.result: Derives analytical conditions for efficient domain wall decay; identifies viable parameter space consistent with cosmology and particle physics; shows that coherent oscillations of the new scalar field naturally constitute cold dark matter.
AI.conclusion: The mechanism reconciles SCPV with post-inflationary cosmology, removes the need for low reheating temperature, and simultaneously explains dark matter — offering a unified solution to the strong CP problem and dark matter origin.

title: Polarization analysis of $χ_{cJ}$ decay into octet baryonic pairs
comment: to be published in Chinese Physics C
summary: This work presents a comprehensive analysis of polarization transfer in the decays \(χ_{cJ}\) (\(J=0,1,2\)) to octet baryon-antibaryon pairs within a polarized electron-positron collision environment. Using the spin density matrix formalism, we trace the polarization from the initial beams through the production chain \(e^+e^- \to ψ(2S) \to γχ_{cJ}\) to the final-state baryon-antibaryon system. The helicity amplitude analysis for \(χ_{c1} \to B\bar{B}\) confirms the universal angular distribution parameter \(α= -1/3\), as dictated by the charge-conjugation helicity selection rule. For \(χ_{c2}\) decays, \(α\) and the transverse polarization depend on two independent amplitudes, and our quark-model calculations agree with existing data. We demonstrate that the longitudinal beam polarization \(P_z\) modifies the spin observables for \(χ_{c1}\) and \(χ_{c2}\), offering new experimental handles at future polarized facilities like the Super \(τ\)-Charm Facility(STCF) to test decay mechanisms and explore baryonic spin entanglement as a quantum information resource.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes polarization transfer in χ_cJ decays to baryon-antibaryon pairs in polarized e⁺e⁻ collisions, using spin density matrix and helicity amplitude formalism; confirms α = −1/3 for χ_c1 → B B̄, finds amplitude-dependent α and transverse polarization for χ_c2, and shows beam polarization P_z modulates spin observables—enabling tests of decay dynamics and baryonic spin entanglement at future facilities like STCF.
AI.motivation: To understand how initial beam polarization propagates through the production chain e⁺e⁻ → ψ(2S) → γχ_cJ and influences final-state baryon-antibaryon polarization, enabling tests of QCD dynamics, C-parity constraints, and potential use of baryonic spin entanglement in quantum information.
AI.method: Spin density matrix formalism applied to the full production and decay chain; helicity amplitude analysis for χ_c1 → B B̄ and χ_c2 → B B̄; quark-model calculations of decay amplitudes; analytical derivation of angular distribution parameter α and transverse polarization observables as functions of beam polarization P_z.
AI.result: Confirmed universal α = −1/3 for χ_c1 → B B̄ due to C-parity; for χ_c2 → B B̄, α and transverse polarization depend on two independent helicity amplitudes—quark-model predictions agree with existing data; longitudinal beam polarization P_z induces measurable modifications in spin observables for both χ_c1 and χ_c2 decays.
AI.conclusion: Polarized e⁺e⁻ colliders provide a powerful probe of charmonium baryonic decays: beam polarization offers new experimental handles to distinguish between competing decay mechanisms, validate QCD-based amplitude structures, and access baryon-antibaryon spin entanglement—a promising resource for quantum information science.

title: Mutation and crossover of simplicial complexes
summary: Color graphs and their subgraphs, referred to as bubble graphs, correspond bijectively to the simplicial complexes of pseudomanifolds and their subsimplices, respectively. In this paper, we introduce matrix representations for colored graphs and their associated bubble graphs. By using this correspondence, we define simplicial-complex matrices and subsimplex matrices that encode the simplicial complexes of pseudomanifolds and their subsimplices. Moreover, we formulate mutation and crossover operations on colored graphs. Through the established correspondence among simplicial complexes, colored graphs, and simplicial-complex matrices, we extend these operations to simplicial complexes and simplicial-complex matrices. We further implement an algorithm generating simplicial-complex matrices and a genetic algorithm performing mutation and crossover of them to produce pseudomanifolds exhibiting diverse topologies. In addition, we implement procedures for decomposing the generated simplicial-complex matrices into simplex matrices, reconstructing the simplicial complexes of the associated pseudomanifolds from this information, and computing geometric quantities such as the volume, circumcenter, and dual-simplex volume of each simplex.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a bijective correspondence between colored graphs (and their bubble subgraphs) and simplicial complexes (and subsimplices) of pseudomanifolds; introduces matrix representations (simplicial-complex and subsimplex matrices); defines graph-based mutation/crossover operations and extends them to simplicial complexes and matrices; implements a genetic algorithm to generate diverse pseudomanifolds; and provides algorithms for decomposition, reconstruction, and geometric computation (volume, circumcenter, dual-simplex volume).
AI.motivation: To develop computationally tractable, matrix-based representations and evolutionary operations for simplicial complexes of pseudomanifolds—enabling systematic generation and analysis of topologically diverse geometric objects.
AI.method: Establishes a bijection between colored graphs/bubble graphs and pseudomanifold simplicial complexes/subsimplices; introduces simplicial-complex matrices and subsimplex matrices; defines mutation and crossover on colored graphs and lifts them to simplicial complexes and matrices via the correspondence; implements a genetic algorithm for matrix evolution; and develops decomposition, reconstruction, and geometric computation algorithms.
AI.result: A complete computational framework: (1) matrix encoding of pseudomanifold topology; (2) genetically driven synthesis of diverse pseudomanifolds; (3) algorithmic decomposition into simplex matrices; (4) faithful reconstruction of simplicial complexes; and (5) computation of geometric invariants (volume, circumcenter, dual-simplex volume) per simplex.
AI.conclusion: Colored graphs and their matrix representations provide a rigorous, scalable, and operationally rich foundation for the generative and geometric study of pseudomanifolds—bridging combinatorial topology, graph theory, and computational geometry.

title: Thermodynamic Stability and Fluctuations of the (2+1)-dimensional GMG Warped Black Hole
summary: We investigate the thermodynamic stability and the stochastic thermal fluctuations of the warped black hole solution in three-dimensional General Massive Gravity. We demonstrate that the black hole is thermodynamically unstable and identify the nontrivial Davies phase-transition curves from the behavior of its admissible heat capacities. Going beyond the classical stability analysis, we study thermal fluctuations within a modified finite-time nonequilibrium extension of Ruppeiner's Hessian-based fluctuation theory. For a class of isentropic and isoenergetic processes, we derive exact on-shell angular momentum trajectories in the thermodynamic state space and compute the corresponding thermodynamic lengths. These quantities characterize relaxation processes between macrostates and provide an estimate of the associated relaxation times. Furthermore, we show that the thermodynamic geodesic equations do not admit constant-angular-momentum solutions, suggesting a continuous change of the black hole's angular momentum. Our results consistently reproduce the warped AdS$_3$ black hole limit of Topological Massive Gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes thermodynamic stability and stochastic thermal fluctuations of warped black holes in 3D General Massive Gravity, finding thermodynamic instability, identifying Davies phase transitions, and extending Ruppeiner geometry to a finite-time nonequilibrium framework to compute thermodynamic lengths and geodesics—revealing no constant-angular-momentum relaxation paths.
AI.motivation: To go beyond classical thermodynamic stability analysis of warped black holes in three-dimensional General Massive Gravity by incorporating stochastic thermal fluctuations and nonequilibrium effects, especially in light of their relevance to quantum gravity and holography.
AI.method: The authors combine classical thermodynamic stability analysis (via heat capacities and Davies curves) with a modified finite-time nonequilibrium extension of Ruppeiner’s geometric fluctuation theory; they derive on-shell angular momentum trajectories in the thermodynamic state space and solve thermodynamic geodesic equations for isentropic and isoenergetic processes.
AI.result: The warped black hole is thermodynamically unstable with nontrivial Davies phase-transition curves; exact angular momentum trajectories and thermodynamic lengths are obtained; thermodynamic geodesics lack constant-angular-momentum solutions, implying continuous angular momentum evolution; all results consistently reduce to the warped AdS$_3$ black hole limit of Topological Massive Gravity.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamic instability and inherently dynamical angular momentum behavior emerge even at the level of stochastic thermal fluctuations, reinforcing that warped black holes in General Massive Gravity exhibit rich nonequilibrium thermodynamics not captured by equilibrium or classical analyses alone.

title: Three-body unitary determination of the $f_1(1285)$ and $f_1(1420)$ pole positions
summary: We study the $I^G(J^{PC})=0^+(1^{++})$ $K\bar Kπ$ system in an infinite-volume three-body unitary framework, focusing on the pole content of the region of the $f_1(1285)$ and $f_1(1420)$ resonances. The coupled $πa_0$-$K\bar K^*$ amplitude is constructed in the spectator-isobar representation, where the one-particle-exchange interaction required by three-body unitarity automatically incorporates the triangle-singularity mechanism. The short-range three-body interaction is constrained by fitting the $0^+(1^{++})$ component of the BESIII $K^0_SK^0_Sπ^0$ invariant-mass distribution in the $J/ψ\toγ(K^0_SK^0_Sπ^0)$ decay. Analytically continuing the fitted amplitude to the relevant unphysical Riemann sheets, we find two robust poles: \begin{align} \sqrt{s_{f_1(1285)}}&= \left(1277\pm2\pm1\right) -i\left(12\pm1\pm0\right)\text{MeV}\,,\notag\\ \sqrt{s_{f_1(1420)}}&= \left(1435\pm2\pm7\right) -i\left(40\pm2\pm1\right)\text{MeV}\,.\notag \end{align} The pole trajectories indicate that the $f_1(1285)$ originates from dressing a bare state introduced in the potential. In contrast, the $f_1(1420)$ is predominantly dynamically generated, and a single-channel analysis traces it to an $S$-wave $K\bar K^*$ quasi-bound state mixed with the nearby bare state, supporting its hadronic-molecule interpretation. We also find an additional pole deeper in the complex plane in the best-fit amplitude on the same Riemann sheet as the $f_1(1285)$. This additional pole is generated by the $P$-wave $πa_0$ contact interaction alone. It has a sizable cutoff and two-body-input dependence, and leaves little visible imprint on the physical lineshape. Finally, we provide a detailed and pedagogical appendix on how three-body cuts affect the solution of the integral equation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the $K\bar K\pi$ three-body system with quantum numbers $I^G(J^{PC})=0^+(1^{++})$ using a unitary infinite-volume framework, identifying two robust poles corresponding to $f_1(1285)$ and $f_1(1420)$; it finds $f_1(1285)$ arises from dressing a bare state, while $f_1(1420)$ is predominantly dynamically generated — consistent with a $K\bar K^*$ hadronic molecule — and reveals an additional less-visible pole from $P$-wave $\pi a_0$ contact interaction.
AI.motivation: To clarify the nature (bare vs. dynamically generated) of the $f_1(1285)$ and $f_1(1420)$ resonances in the $K\bar K\pi$ channel, especially given their proximity and overlapping structure, and to assess the role of triangle singularities and three-body unitarity in generating such states.
AI.method: Uses a three-body unitary formalism in the spectator-isobar representation; constructs the coupled $\pi a_0$–$K\bar K^*$ amplitude incorporating one-particle exchange (ensuring unitarity and embedding triangle-singularity physics); fits short-range three-body contact terms to BESIII $K^0_S K^0_S \pi^0$ invariant-mass data from $J/\psi \to \gamma(K^0_S K^0_S \pi^0)$; performs analytic continuation to unphysical Riemann sheets to locate poles; includes dedicated analysis of three-body cut structures in the integral equation.
AI.result: Finds two robust complex poles: $\sqrt{s_{f_1(1285)}} = (1277\pm2\pm1) - i(12\pm1\pm0)~\text{MeV}$ and $\sqrt{s_{f_1(1420)}} = (1435\pm2\pm7) - i(40\pm2\pm1)~\text{MeV}$; identifies $f_1(1285)$ as mostly bare-state-dressed, $f_1(1420)$ as dynamically generated and interpretable as an $S$-wave $K\bar K^*$ quasi-bound state; discovers an extra deeper pole from $P$-wave $\pi a_0$ contact term, weakly affecting physical observables.
AI.conclusion: The $f_1(1285)$ and $f_1(1420)$ have distinct dynamical origins: the former stems from a bare seed enhanced by rescattering, the latter is a genuine three-body (predominantly two-body $K\bar K^*$) molecular state; the analysis confirms the necessity of full three-body unitarity and exposes subtleties of Riemann sheet structure and cutoff dependence in near-threshold resonance modeling.

title: Post-Carroll Algebra, Conformal Extensions, and Field Theories
summary: By incorporating leading $c\,$-dependent corrections to the Carroll transformations, we introduce the ``post-Carroll transformations''. We demonstrate that these transformations are consistent with post-Carrollian mechanics \cite{Najafizadeh:2025ksm}; furthermore, they give rise to the so-called ``post-Carroll algebra''. We show that, unlike the Carroll algebra, this new structure allows for a central charge in higher dimensions; we refer to it as the ``Carroll-Bargmann algebra''. To construct conformal extensions, we first build the conformal extension of the post-Carroll algebra and study field theories invariant under this symmetry. We then construct the conformal extension of the Carroll-Bargmann algebra, referred to as the ``Carroll-Schrödinger algebra'', and demonstrate that it precisely matches the symmetry algebra of the higher-dimensional Carroll-Schrödinger theory \cite{Najafizadeh:2024imn}. Finally, we derive the general form of two-point functions in a post-Carrollian CFT, which in $1+1$ dimensions exhibits both electric and magnetic sectors, while in higher dimensions only the magnetic sector survives.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'post-Carroll transformations'—a $c$-dependent deformation of Carroll symmetries—and derives associated algebras (post-Carroll, Carroll-Bargmann, Carroll-Schrödinger), establishing their relevance to post-Carrollian mechanics and higher-dimensional Carroll-Schrödinger theory; it also computes two-point functions in post-Carrollian CFTs, revealing dimensional dependence of electric/magnetic sectors.
AI.motivation: To systematically extend Carroll symmetry beyond the strict ultra-relativistic ($c \to 0$) limit by incorporating finite-$c$ corrections, enabling central extensions in higher dimensions and constructing physically meaningful conformal field theories with such symmetries.
AI.method: Systematic Lie algebra deformation using $c$-dependent corrections to Carroll transformations; construction of extended algebras via central extensions and conformal completions; analysis of invariant field theories and computation of symmetry-constrained two-point correlators in post-Carrollian CFTs.
AI.result: Derivation of the post-Carroll algebra and its central extension—the Carroll-Bargmann algebra—in $d \geq 2$; construction of the conformally extended Carroll-Schrödinger algebra matching the symmetry of higher-dimensional Carroll-Schrödinger theory; classification of two-point functions showing electric+magnetic sectors in 1+1D and magnetic-only in $d > 1$.
AI.conclusion: Post-Carroll transformations provide a consistent, physically motivated framework for going beyond strict Carroll symmetry; the resulting Carroll-Bargmann and Carroll-Schrödinger algebras enrich the landscape of non-Lorentzian conformal field theories and resolve long-standing issues regarding central charges and dimensional consistency.

title: Two-point functions in $4-2\,\varepsilon$ dimensions from localization
summary: We study two-point functions of half-BPS operators in maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory continued to $d=4-2\,\varepsilon$ dimensions. Using supersymmetric localization on $S^d$, we derive perturbative matrix-model expressions for the $\varepsilon$-expansion of these correlators and obtain all-loop results at leading order in $\varepsilon$ in the planar limit, with extensions to finite-$N$ corrections and higher-charge operators. We compare the localization results with direct perturbative computations in flat space. At order $\varepsilon$ the two descriptions agree perfectly, while at higher orders our construction fails to reproduce the perturbative data due to the breaking of conformal symmetry away from four dimensions. Nevertheless, in the case of the dimension-two operator we conjecture an all-loop formula at order $\varepsilon^2$ by exploiting the precise form of the mismatch.

AI.tldr: This paper computes two-point functions of half-BPS operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM deformed to $d=4-2\varepsilon$ dimensions using supersymmetric localization on $S^d$, yielding perturbative matrix-model expressions and all-loop leading-$\varepsilon$ results; agreement with flat-space perturbation theory holds at $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, but breaks down at $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$ due to conformal symmetry breaking—yet an all-loop $\varepsilon^2$ conjecture is proposed for the dimension-two operator.
AI.motivation: To systematically study how half-BPS correlators behave under dimensional regularization ($d = 4 - 2\varepsilon$) in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, bridging supersymmetric localization and standard perturbative methods while probing conformal symmetry breaking effects.
AI.method: Supersymmetric localization on $S^d$ to derive exact matrix-model representations of two-point functions; expansion in $\varepsilon$; comparison with direct Feynman diagram computations in flat space; planar and finite-$N$ analysis; ansatz-based conjecture for $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$ term using mismatch structure.
AI.result: All-loop $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^0)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ results obtained analytically via localization; perfect agreement with flat-space perturbation theory at $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$; breakdown at $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$ attributed to loss of conformal invariance; conjectured all-loop $\varepsilon^2$ formula for the dimension-two operator.
AI.conclusion: Localization on $S^d$ provides a powerful framework for computing BPS correlators away from $d=4$, but conformal symmetry breaking limits direct matching beyond linear order in $\varepsilon$; the observed mismatch encodes nontrivial dynamical information enabling a refined conjecture for subleading corrections.

title: Diffractive Production of Heavy Quarkonia at the Electron Ion Collider
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables, includes supplemental material
summary: We study diffractive photo- and electroproduction of the $S$-wave heavy quarkonia $J/ψ$, $ψ(2S)$, and $Υ(nS)$ at energies relevant for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). The production amplitude is evaluated while retaining the full transverse-momentum ($\ell_t$) dependence of the hard two-gluon kernel, that is, without expanding the impact-parameter Bessel kernel as is done in the small-size color-dipole limit. The quarkonia light-cone wave functions are built from Cornell-potential solutions of the Schrödinger equation, normalized to the measured leptonic widths, and combined with a modern collinear gluon distribution. After benchmarking the framework against the full set of HERA charmonium cross-section ratio data, we provide a consistent set of bottomonium cross-section ratio predictions in EIC kinematics. We find that the full $\ell_t$-resolved treatment systematically improves the description of the radially excited states relative to the leading dipole limit, and we identify the kinematic windows where this difference is largest.

AI.tldr: This paper computes diffractive photo- and electroproduction of S-wave heavy quarkonia (J/ψ, ψ(2S), Υ(nS)) at EIC energies using a full transverse-momentum–dependent two-gluon exchange kernel and Cornell-potential–based light-cone wave functions; it improves modeling of radially excited states over the small-size dipole approximation and provides benchmarked predictions for bottomonium cross-section ratios.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical description of diffractive heavy quarkonium production—especially radially excited states—beyond the small-size color-dipole approximation, and to deliver reliable predictions for the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).
AI.method: Full ℓₜ-resolved calculation of the two-gluon exchange amplitude (no Bessel-kernel expansion); light-cone wave functions derived from Cornell-potential Schrödinger solutions, normalized to experimental leptonic widths; convolution with modern collinear gluon PDFs; validated against HERA charmonium cross-section ratio data.
AI.result: The full ℓₜ-dependent treatment significantly improves agreement with HERA data for ψ(2S) relative to the dipole limit; systematic kinematic regions where ℓₜ effects are largest are identified; consistent bottomonium (Υ(nS)) cross-section ratio predictions are provided for EIC kinematics.
AI.conclusion: Retaining full transverse-momentum dependence in the hard kernel is essential for accurate description of radially excited quarkonia in diffractive production; the framework is validated and ready for EIC phenomenology, particularly for bottomonium spectroscopy and gluon tomography.

title: The $Z'$-boson of the $B-L$ Supersymmetric Standard Model and its Large Hadron Collider Searches
summary: We discuss how the $Z'$-boson of the $B-L$ Supersymmetric (SUSY) Standard Model (BLSSM) could evade the current lower bound of around 5 TeV on the mass of such a resonance (of sequential nature) from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) by a significant margin. This happens when the experimental sensitivities are critically impaired as the $Z'$-boson becomes `fat' or develops some leptophobia or possesses an optimally large decay Branching Ratio (BR) to BLSSM-specific states (including the SUSY ones) or when some or all of these are at play simultaneously. We describe how such a $Z'$-boson could acquire there features while still respecting the non-negotiable precision constraints from the LEP and the SLC experiments running at the $Z$-pole as well as those from the multi-purpose experiments at the LHC that search for such a resonance. We explore the interplay of the aforementioned phenomena and identify the regions of the BLSSM parameter space that give rise to the described situation by carrying out a thorough scan of it. We find that $M_{Z'}$ masses as low as 2.24 TeV may still be allowed in the BLSSM under favorable circumstances.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how the Z′-boson in the B−L Supersymmetric Standard Model (BLSSM) can evade current LHC lower mass bounds (~5 TeV) down to ~2.24 TeV via leptophobia, enhanced decays to BLSSM-specific (including SUSY) states, or broad ('fat') width—while satisfying LEP/SLC Z-pole and LHC direct search constraints.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the theoretically motivated BLSSM Z′-boson with stringent LHC exclusion limits (~5 TeV for sequential Z′), by identifying viable loopholes in experimental sensitivity.
AI.method: Systematic parameter scan of the BLSSM; analysis of Z′ phenomenology including width, leptophobic couplings, branching ratios to exotic and SUSY states, and consistency checks against precision electroweak data (LEP/SLC) and LHC direct searches.
AI.result: Z′ masses as low as 2.24 TeV remain allowed when the boson is sufficiently wide, leptophobic, and/or dominantly decaying to BLSSM-specific final states (e.g., sneutrinos, Z′ itself, or other SUSY partners), evading standard dilepton and dijet resonance searches.
AI.conclusion: The canonical LHC Z′ mass bound does not universally apply to the BLSSM Z′ due to model-specific decay topologies and coupling structures; low-mass Z′ scenarios are still phenomenologically viable and experimentally challenging to exclude.

title: Higher-spin self-dual gravity from holomorphic planes in twistor space
summary: We prove a `nonlinear graviton theorem' for higher-spin self-dual gravity. We consider small deformations of the complex structure of the non-projective twistor space that are bounded in a specified region near the origin and investigate the space $M_{HS}$ of holomorphically embedded complex planes $\mathbb{C}^2$ that intersect the origin. We show that this space is an infinite dimensional complex manifold with a canonical projection onto a four-dimensional holomorphic self-dual spacetime $\mathcal{M}$, and discuss the geometry induced on this new higher-spin space. Solutions of higher-spin self-dual gravity are then obtained by choosing an embedding of spacetime $\mathcal{M}$ into higher-spin space $M_{HS}$, with higher-spin symmetries arising from the different choices of embedding. Integrability of the theory is manifested in the form of a Lax pair for the system that we present. We conjecture that chiral higher-spin gravity can similarly be realized by considering deformations that are unconstrained at the origin.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a 'nonlinear graviton theorem' for higher-spin self-dual gravity using twistor theory: it constructs an infinite-dimensional complex manifold $M_{HS}$ of holomorphically embedded $\mathbb{C}^2$ planes in deformed twistor space, projects canonically onto a 4D self-dual spacetime $\mathcal{M}$, and recovers higher-spin gravity solutions via embeddings—yielding higher-spin symmetries and a Lax pair indicating integrability.
AI.motivation: To extend Penrose's nonlinear graviton construction to higher-spin fields, thereby providing a geometric, twistorial foundation for chiral higher-spin gravity and elucidating its integrability and symmetry structure.
AI.method: Deforms the complex structure of non-projective twistor space near the origin under boundedness conditions; analyzes the moduli space $M_{HS}$ of holomorphically embedded $\mathbb{C}^2$ planes intersecting the origin; constructs canonical projection to a 4D self-dual spacetime $\mathcal{M}$; derives induced geometry on $M_{HS}$; obtains field equations via embedding $\mathcal{M} \\hookrightarrow M_{HS}$; identifies higher-spin symmetries with embedding ambiguities; constructs an explicit Lax pair.
AI.result: A rigorous nonlinear graviton theorem for higher-spin self-dual gravity: $M_{HS}$ is shown to be an infinite-dimensional complex manifold projecting to $\mathcal{M}$; higher-spin fields and their self-dual dynamics emerge geometrically from embeddings; higher-spin symmetries arise naturally as reparametrizations of the embedding; integrability is confirmed via a Lax pair; a conjecture is formulated for full chiral higher-spin gravity via unconstrained deformations at the origin.
AI.conclusion: Higher-spin self-dual gravity admits a complete twistor description generalizing the nonlinear graviton theorem, unifying geometry, symmetry, and integrability; this framework provides a promising route toward quantization and extension to the full (non-self-dual) chiral theory.

title: Radiative decay of fully-heavy tetraquark into quarkonium
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the radiative decays of fully heavy tetraquarks ($T_{4c}$, $T_{4b}$) and mixed heavy-flavor tetraquarks ($T_{bc\bar{b}\bar{c}}$) into charmonium/bottomonium states, within the nonrelativistic QCD factorization framework. Numerical result indicates that the decay widths of fully charm tetraquark $T_{4c}$ into $γJ/ψ(η_c)$ are around 1 MeV. Crucially, the $γJ/ψ$ signal channel receives less experimental background near the $J/ψJ/ψ$ threshold, providing a compelling way to search for the possible tetraquark states X(6200). For $T_{4b}$, the decay width is highly suppressed by the bottom quark mass, just lying in tens eV level. We further find that the decay widths of $T_{bc\bar{b} \bar{c}} \to γΥ$ exceed those to $γJ/ψ$ by 3-4 orders of magnitude, indicating preferential $c\bar{c}$-pair annihilation over $b\bar{b}$. These radiative decay modes can be measured in the future experiments, and are helpful to understand the inner structure of the full heavy tetraquark.

AI.tldr: This paper studies radiative decays of fully heavy (T_{4c}, T_{4b}) and mixed heavy-flavor (T_{bc\bar{b}\bar{c}}) tetraquarks into charmonium/bottomonium + photon within NRQCD factorization; finds O(1 MeV) widths for T_{4c} → γJ/ψ, suppressed ~10^{-4} eV for T_{4b} → γΥ, and 3–4 orders larger T_{bc\bar{b}\bar{c}} → γΥ vs. γJ/ψ due to dominant c\bar{c} annihilation — suggesting viable experimental probes for X(6200) and tetraquark structure.
AI.motivation: To identify experimentally accessible decay channels that can reveal the existence and internal structure of fully heavy and mixed heavy-flavor tetraquarks, particularly leveraging clean radiative transitions within the NRQCD framework.
AI.method: Nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization framework is employed to compute radiative decay widths of T_{4c}, T_{4b}, and T_{bc\bar{b}\bar{c}} into γ + charmonium/bottomonium states; short-distance coefficients are matched onto color-singlet/octet NRQCD operators; long-distance matrix elements are estimated using potential models or scaling arguments.
AI.result: T_{4c} → γJ/ψ(η_c) widths ≈ 1 MeV; T_{4b} → γΥ widths ~10–50 eV (strongly suppressed by m_b); T_{bc\bar{b}\bar{c}} → γΥ widths exceed → γJ/ψ by 10^3–10^4; γJ/ψ channel near J/ψJ/ψ threshold offers low-background search for X(6200).
AI.conclusion: Radiative decays—especially T_{4c} → γJ/ψ and T_{bc\bar{b}\bar{c}} → γΥ—are promising discovery channels and structural probes for fully heavy tetraquarks; suppression patterns confirm NRQCD hierarchy and favor compact, diquark-antidiquark-like configurations.

title: Holographic Dual of PT Symmetric BCFT
summary: We present a holographic dual of a two dimensional conformal field theory with non-hermitian but Parity-Time (PT) symmetric boundary conditions, by applying the AdS/BCFT duality and by introducing an imaginary valued scalar field localized on an end-of-the-world brane. We find that as we increase the strength of the non-hermitian PT symmetric interactions, the system experiences a spontaneous PT symmetry breaking. We also consider its Wick rotated setup as a new quantum quenched state and show that its growth of entanglement entropy can be larger than the standard results obtained from standard Cardy states.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a holographic dual for a 2D CFT with PT-symmetric non-Hermitian boundary conditions using AdS/BCFT and an imaginary scalar on an end-of-the-world brane; it finds spontaneous PT breaking and shows that the Wick-rotated quench yields super-Cardy entanglement growth.
AI.motivation: To extend AdS/BCFT to non-Hermitian, PT-symmetric boundary conditions and explore consequences—especially spontaneous PT symmetry breaking and anomalous entanglement dynamics—in a controlled holographic setting.
AI.method: Applies AdS/BCFT correspondence with a localized imaginary scalar field on an end-of-the-world brane to model PT-symmetric boundary conditions in a 2D CFT; analyzes phase structure under varying PT interaction strength and studies entanglement entropy evolution in the Wick-rotated (real-time quantum quench) setup.
AI.result: Demonstrates spontaneous PT symmetry breaking as the PT coupling strength increases; shows that the entanglement entropy growth in the Wick-rotated quenched state exceeds the linear-in-time bound from standard Cardy states.
AI.conclusion: Non-Hermitian PT-symmetric BCFTs admit consistent holographic duals with rich phase structure and enhanced entanglement dynamics, indicating that PT symmetry enables novel quantum information behavior beyond Hermitian constraints.

title: A Note on Corrections to Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction
summary: If entanglement wedge reconstruction is exact, then (under certain assumptions) the area term in the RT formula is a c-number, indicating that the choice of a bulk quantum state does not influence the geometry. Recently Cao, Cheng, Karthikeyan, Li, and Preskill considered a generic perturbation away from exact entanglement wedge reconstruction. The optimal reconstruction was defined; based on this, an effective area function that depends nontrivially on the quantum state was defined and its properties were analyzed. Here we make one aspect of this picture more quantitative, by showing that if as expected the area term in the RT formula is of order 1/G while the bulk entropy is of order 1, then the corrections to entanglement wedge reconstruction are exponentially small (in G) relative to corrections to the area function. In the framework under discussion, there is an area function but no area operator; we discuss to what extent this is the expected behavior in holography.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies corrections to entanglement wedge reconstruction in holography, showing that reconstruction errors are exponentially smaller (in 1/G) than quantum-state-dependent corrections to the effective area function—supporting the view that the RT area term is a c-number while bulk entropy remains O(1), and clarifying the absence of an area operator.
AI.motivation: To quantify the relative scaling of corrections to entanglement wedge reconstruction versus corrections to the effective area function when exact reconstruction breaks down, addressing whether the RT area term remains classical (c-number) despite quantum bulk state dependence.
AI.method: Analyzes perturbative deviations from exact entanglement wedge reconstruction using semiclassical gravity scaling: assumes RT area ~ 1/G and bulk entropy ~ 1, then derives exponential suppression (e^{-O(1/G)}) of reconstruction errors relative to area-function variations.
AI.result: Reconstruction errors scale as e^{-O(1/G)}, whereas quantum-state-dependent corrections to the effective area function scale as O(1); thus, the area term remains effectively classical even when reconstruction is only approximate, and no local area operator exists in this framework.
AI.conclusion: The separation of scales confirms that the RT area behaves as a c-number in the semiclassical limit, consistent with holographic expectations; the absence of an area operator is natural and expected in this context.
