title: Universal Closed Form for Dynamical Love Numbers of Black Holes
summary: Black hole static Love numbers vanish, but their dynamical counterparts do not. We present the scheme-independent dynamical response $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}$ of a Schwarzschild black hole in closed form, to all orders, and for every spin $s$ and multipole $\ell$. The result is $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}/4πR_S^{2\ell+1}=Φ_{\ell,s}(\bar{y})-\tfrac12η\,Φ_{\ell,s}'(\bar{y})$ with $\bar{y}=-\tfrac12η^2τ$ and $η=iωR_S$. Here $Φ_{\ell,s}$ is simply the leading-log solution to the renormalization group equation, but lifting the running logarithm to $τ=\log(R_S/R)-2\sum_{k\ge2}ζ_k\,η^{k-1}$ resums it to all orders. This tower of Riemann zeta values is the Newtonian phase in disguise: it originates from the same far-zone $Γ(1-η)$ that governs long-range scattering, and is universal across multipole and spin. Our result exhibits a factorization pinned to three ingredients: the hard matching coefficient at the horizon, the anomalous dimension in the near zone, and the dressed log in the far zone. Using shell effective field theory, we independently verify our formula for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations, reaching $\mathcal O(G^{15})$.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a scheme-independent, all-order closed-form expression for the dynamical tidal response (Love numbers) of a Schwarzschild black hole for arbitrary spin s and multipole ℓ, revealing universal zeta-valued structure tied to far-zone scattering physics and verified up to O(G¹⁵) via shell EFT.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguity in defining dynamical black hole Love numbers and provide a physically meaningful, scheme-independent, all-orders expression that captures the full frequency-dependent tidal response beyond the static limit where Love numbers vanish.
AI.method: Uses renormalization group (RG) techniques in effective field theory: identifies the dynamical response as governed by a leading-log RG solution Φ_{ℓ,s}, lifts the logarithm via a dressed scale τ containing Riemann zeta values, and factorizes the result into horizon matching, near-zone anomalous dimension, and far-zone dressed log; cross-validated with shell EFT for scalar, EM, and gravitational perturbations up to O(G¹⁵).
AI.result: Derives exact closed-form dynamical response function F̄_{ℓ,s}/4πR_S^{2ℓ+1} = Φ_{ℓ,s}(ȳ) − ½η Φ'_{ℓ,s}(ȳ), where ȳ = −½η²τ, η = iωR_S, and τ = log(R_S/R) − 2∑_{k≥2} ζ_k η^{k−1}; reveals universal appearance of Riemann zeta values as disguised Newtonian phase from far-zone Γ(1−η) factor.
AI.conclusion: Dynamical black hole tidal response is fully determined by a universal, factorized structure involving horizon, near-zone, and far-zone physics; the zeta-valued dressing of the logarithm encodes long-range scattering data and ensures scheme independence to all orders in perturbation theory.

title: Renormalization of the SMEFT to Dimension Eight: Fermionic Interactions II
summary: We compute the one-loop mixing of bosonic and two-fermion interactions into two-fermion operators in the dimension-eight Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Together with the results in arXiv:2106.05291, arXiv:2205.03301, arXiv:2409.15408, and arXiv:2512.21724, this leaves only the mixing of four-fermion operators into two-fermion ones as the remaining piece to complete the SMEFT renormalization program at this order.

AI.tldr: This paper computes one-loop mixing of bosonic and two-fermion dimension-eight SMEFT operators into two-fermion operators, completing all but the four-fermion → two-fermion mixing in the dimension-eight SMEFT renormalization program.
AI.motivation: To complete the renormalization program of the dimension-eight Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at one-loop order.
AI.method: Perturbative quantum field theory computation of one-loop anomalous dimensions, specifically evaluating operator mixing from bosonic and two-fermion dimension-eight operators into two-fermion ones.
AI.result: The one-loop mixing coefficients for bosonic and two-fermion → two-fermion operator transitions at dimension eight are fully computed.
AI.conclusion: Only the four-fermion → two-fermion mixing remains to be calculated to finalize the one-loop renormalization of the dimension-eight SMEFT.

title: SUSY meets pseudo-Hermiticity
summary: In this work, we construct the simplest pseudo-Hermitian quantum field theory that is supersymmetric. This is the pseudo-Hermitian Wess-Zumino model in the sense that it contains a pair of symplectic fermions (anti-commuting scalar fields) that satisfy the Klein-Gordon equation and a spin-half boson that satisfies the Dirac equation. The conventional spin-statistics theorem is circumvented through the use of pseudo-Hermitian conjugation to define field adjoints. To make the supersymmetry manifest, we formulate the pseudo-Hermitian Wess-Zumino model using the superfield formalism. These superfields are Grassmann-odd so it is not possible to construct non-vanishing cubic interactions using only these superfields. We show that this problem can be resolved by coupling the pseudo-Hermitian Wess-Zumino model with the Hermitian Wess-Zumino model while preserving supersymmetry.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the simplest pseudo-Hermitian, supersymmetric quantum field theory—the pseudo-Hermitian Wess-Zumino model—using symplectic fermions and a spin-half boson, bypassing the spin-statistics theorem via pseudo-Hermitian conjugation; manifest supersymmetry is achieved via Grassmann-odd superfields, and viable cubic interactions are enabled by coupling to the Hermitian Wess-Zumino model while preserving supersymmetry.
AI.motivation: To construct a consistent, supersymmetric quantum field theory that is pseudo-Hermitian (enabling non-Hermitian yet unitary dynamics) while evading the constraints of the standard spin-statistics theorem.
AI.method: Formulates a pseudo-Hermitian Wess-Zumino model with symplectic fermions and a spin-half boson; employs pseudo-Hermitian conjugation for field adjoints; uses Grassmann-odd superfields in superfield formalism to make supersymmetry manifest; resolves absence of cubic interactions by supersymmetrically coupling to the Hermitian Wess-Zumino model.
AI.result: A well-defined, supersymmetric pseudo-Hermitian QFT is constructed; the spin-statistics theorem is circumvented without breaking unitarity or locality; cubic interactions are enabled via a supersymmetric hybrid model.
AI.conclusion: The pseudo-Hermitian Wess-Zumino model—augmented by coupling to its Hermitian counterpart—provides a consistent, minimal framework for supersymmetric, pseudo-Hermitian quantum field theory, broadening the scope of viable non-Hermitian extensions of the Standard Model.

title: Spectral Functions of Lorentzian Quantum Gravity
summary: We compute spectral functions of graviton modes in Lorentzian quantum gravity, interpolating between classical general relativity and an asymptotically safe ultraviolet fixed point. Using functional renormalisation adapted for theories in Lorentzian signature, and enhanced by new symmetry conditions to account for underlying Ward identities, we derive and solve flow equations directly for the Källén-Lehmann representation of propagators. Consistent results are found for several sets of renormalisation conditions yielding normalisable spectral functions for the graviton and the scalar graviton mode, in agreement with effective theory in the infrared. We further calculate the full quantum effective action to quadratic order in curvature, extract graviton-induced form factors, and discuss implications for unitarity of quantum gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper computes graviton spectral functions in Lorentzian quantum gravity using functional renormalisation, deriving flow equations for the Källén-Lehmann representation; it finds normalisable spectral functions consistent with IR effective theory and computes curvature-quadratic quantum effective action and form factors to assess unitarity.
AI.motivation: To bridge classical general relativity and asymptotically safe quantum gravity in Lorentzian signature, and to assess unitarity via spectral properties of graviton modes.
AI.method: Functional renormalisation group (FRG) adapted to Lorentzian signature, augmented with symmetry constraints enforcing Ward identities; derivation and numerical solution of flow equations for the Källén-Lehmann spectral representation of graviton propagators; computation of the quantum effective action to quadratic order in curvature and extraction of graviton-induced form factors.
AI.result: Normalisable spectral functions for both tensor (graviton) and scalar graviton modes across RG scales; consistency with infrared effective theory; explicit form factors encoding quantum corrections to gravitational interactions.
AI.conclusion: The existence of well-behaved, normalisable spectral functions supports UV completeness and perturbative unitarity in asymptotically safe quantum gravity; the framework provides a robust, signature-aware route to test unitarity beyond Euclidean approximations.

title: ASEP/DSSYK duality and strange correlator
summary: We show that the moment of the transfer matrix of the double scaled SYK model is written as an overlap between the stationary state of ASEP (asymmetric simple exclusion process) and a product state. We argue that this overlap is an analogue of the strange correlator appearing in the correspondence between the Levin-Wen string-net model and the Turaev-Viro state sum.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a connection between the double-scaled SYK model's transfer matrix moments and an overlap in the ASEP, drawing an analogy to the strange correlator in Levin-Wen/Turaev-Viro correspondence.
AI.motivation: To uncover hidden integrable structures and dualities linking quantum many-body systems (SYK), stochastic processes (ASEP), and topological quantum field theories (Turaev-Viro).
AI.method: Analytical mapping of the moment generating function of the SYK transfer matrix onto an ASEP stationary-state overlap; conceptual analogy with strange correlators in topological lattice models.
AI.result: A precise identification of SYK transfer matrix moments as overlaps between the ASEP stationary state and a product state; interpretation as a 'strange correlator'-like object bridging random matrix theory and integrable stochastic processes.
AI.conclusion: The double-scaled SYK model exhibits an unexpected correspondence with ASEP, suggesting deeper links between quantum chaos, non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, and topological quantum order via strange correlator analogues.

title: Hydrodynamics of perfect fluids with anomalies from the fermionic path integral
summary: The path integral of the Dirac fermion with vector and axial gauge backgrounds is analyzed near the infrared limit in the presence of residual irrelevant current-current interaction. After integrating out fermions, a semiclassical low-energy effective action is obtained, written in terms of currents. Its expression is found to correspond to the hydrodynamic action previously proposed for perfect barotropic fluids with anomalies at zero temperature. This approach also leads to two further hydrodynamic actions to be associated, respectively, with the Weyl fermion, and the Dirac fermion having independent vector and axial currents. These actions feature four- and five-dimensional bulk-boundary terms, owing to anomaly inflow, which are identified as being the so-called transgression forms. These are generalizations of Chern--Simons forms that involve two gauge fields: the dynamical field and the background field. The path-integral argument provides a ``microscopic'' explanation for several ingredients of the action formulation of hydrodynamics that are necessary to incorporate anomalies. It also clarifies the infrared reduction required to pass from the effective field theory to a local hydrodynamic description. This reduction is implemented by considering restricted variations of the action, familiar from hydrodynamics, which at the same time lead to four-dimensional equations of motion from the five-dimensional transgression terms.

AI.tldr: This paper derives hydrodynamic effective actions for anomalous quantum fluids (Dirac/Weyl fermions) from a path-integral treatment of fermions coupled to vector/axial gauge fields, identifying transgression forms—generalized Chern–Simons terms—as the anomaly-inflow origin of bulk-boundary couplings in hydrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To provide a microscopic, path-integral-based derivation of anomaly-compatible hydrodynamic effective actions, clarifying the infrared reduction from quantum field theory to local hydrodynamics and explaining the origin of transgression-type bulk-boundary terms.
AI.method: Path-integral quantization of Dirac and Weyl fermions with vector and axial gauge backgrounds; integration over fermionic degrees of freedom in the infrared limit; semiclassical expansion yielding current-based low-energy effective actions; identification of transgression forms via anomaly inflow.
AI.result: Derivation of three hydrodynamic effective actions: one for Dirac fermions with vector/axial backgrounds (matching known perfect barotropic fluid action), and two novel ones for Weyl fermions and Dirac fermions with independent vector/axial currents—each containing 4D/5D transgression terms encoding anomaly inflow.
AI.conclusion: The path-integral approach microscopically justifies the structure of anomalous hydrodynamic actions, establishes transgression forms as the natural geometric realization of anomaly inflow in hydrodynamics, and shows that restricted variational principles implement the IR reduction to local hydrodynamic equations—even when the action is higher-dimensional.

title: Higher-Trace Operators and Cut Diagrammatics in the Conformal Block Expansion
summary: We study four-point functions of identical scalar operators in conformal field theories with AdS duals in large-$N$ expansion. We analyze the appearance of higher-trace operators in theories dual to bulk $φ^3$ and $φ^4$ interactions, focusing on how these operators are required by crossing symmetry. We compute part of the OPE data associated with these operators. We also introduce a diagrammatic framework for organizing the different terms in the conformal block expansion within the large-$N$ expansion. This framework refines the use of crossing symmetry by allowing it to be applied to individual diagrammatic topologies, rather than only to the full correlator. It further separates different contributions to the OPE data by associating them with different cut diagrams. In this language, the emergence of higher-trace operators and their relation to lower-trace OPE data become more manifest.

AI.tldr: This paper studies four-point functions of identical scalars in large-N CFTs with AdS duals, focusing on higher-trace operators required by crossing symmetry in φ³ and φ⁴ bulk theories; it computes partial OPE data and introduces a diagrammatic framework that organizes conformal block expansions by topology and associates OPE contributions with cut diagrams.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher-trace operators arise from crossing symmetry in large-N CFTs with weakly coupled AdS duals, and to systematically organize OPE data beyond the leading order in 1/N.
AI.method: Conformal bootstrap analysis combined with large-N expansion; explicit computation of OPE coefficients and scaling dimensions for higher-trace operators; development of a diagrammatic formalism using cut diagrams to classify contributions to the conformal block expansion by topology.
AI.result: Identification of higher-trace operator families necessitated by crossing symmetry in φ³ and φ⁴ bulk interactions; partial analytic results for their anomalous dimensions and OPE coefficients; a refined diagrammatic framework linking specific topologies and cuts to distinct classes of OPE data.
AI.conclusion: Higher-trace operators are not optional but mandated by crossing symmetry in large-N holographic CFTs; the proposed diagrammatic framework enhances precision in applying crossing symmetry—enabling topology-resolved constraints and clarifying the hierarchical relation between lower- and higher-trace OPE data.

title: Instability of 5D Gauss-Bonnet black branes
summary: We show that Gauss-Bonnet black branes in five-dimensional anti-de Sitter gravity are unstable when the Gauss-Bonnet coupling falls outside the range allowed by the conformal collider bounds. The unstable modes and the boundary causality violating modes are connected by a phase rotation of complex boundary momentum.

AI.tldr: Gauss-Bonnet black branes in 5D AdS gravity exhibit instability outside the conformal collider bounds on the Gauss-Bonnet coupling; unstable and boundary causality-violating modes are related by a complex momentum phase rotation.
AI.motivation: To investigate stability of Gauss-Bonnet black branes in five-dimensional anti-de Sitter gravity and its connection to boundary causality constraints from conformal field theory.
AI.method: Analysis of linearized perturbations around Gauss-Bonnet black brane solutions; mapping between bulk quasinormal modes and boundary momentum via analytic continuation in complex momentum space.
AI.result: Instability occurs when the Gauss-Bonnet coupling parameter lies outside the range permitted by conformal collider bounds; unstable quasinormal modes and boundary causality-violating modes are analytically connected through a phase rotation of complex boundary momentum.
AI.conclusion: The conformal collider bounds not only constrain CFT data but also govern classical gravitational stability in the dual bulk, revealing a deep link between boundary causality and bulk instability in higher-curvature gravity.

title: Bubble wall velocity and nucleation rates in inverse holographic phase transitions
summary: We study the dynamics of first-order inverse phase transitions (driven by superheating) at strong coupling, focusing on the top-down Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model for holographic QCD. Two cases are considered: the deconfinement transition in the unflavored version of the model and a chiral symmetry-restoring transition occurring in the deconfined phase of the full theory. In both cases, we imagine driving the system into a metastable phase at high temperature, inducing the nucleation of bubbles of the stable phase. For both classes of transitions, we find the corresponding Euclidean bounce solutions and compute the bubble nucleation rates and the relevant transition parameters. For the deconfinement transition, the large jump in the number of degrees of freedom between the two phases suggests that the bubble wall velocity is parametrically small; we provide a rough estimate of it near the critical temperature. In the case of the chiral transition, instead, we compute the bubble wall velocity and the friction force exerted on the bubbles employing motivated ansatze and approximations for the steady-state configurations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates first-order inverse phase transitions (superheating-driven) in the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto holographic QCD model, computing Euclidean bounce solutions, nucleation rates, and bubble dynamics for both deconfinement and chiral symmetry-restoring transitions.
AI.motivation: To understand non-equilibrium dynamics of first-order inverse phase transitions—specifically superheating-induced transitions—in strongly coupled QCD-like theories using holography, where standard perturbative methods fail.
AI.method: Uses the top-down Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model; constructs and solves Euclidean bounce equations for bubble nucleation; estimates bubble wall velocity and friction via ansatze and hydrodynamic approximations; analyzes thermodynamic and gravitational background data near critical temperature.
AI.result: Obtains explicit bounce solutions and nucleation rates for both deconfinement and chiral transitions; finds parametrically small wall velocity for deconfinement due to large d.o.f. jump; computes finite wall velocity and friction for chiral transition using steady-state approximations.
AI.conclusion: Inverse phase transitions in strongly coupled QCD admit controlled holographic description; bubble dynamics differ qualitatively between deconfinement and chiral transitions, reflecting distinct underlying degrees of freedom and transport properties.

title: A Dispersive Bootstrap for the Virasoro-Shapiro Amplitude
summary: We study the closed-string tree-level Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude using the dispersive S-matrix bootstrap. For the ten-dimensional maximally supersymmetric four-point amplitude, we impose analyticity, crossing symmetry, partial-wave unitarity, and Regge boundedness. With the massless graviton pole kept explicitly, the resulting dispersion relations and crossing null constraints give numerical bounds on the leading low-energy coefficients normalized by the gravitational coupling. We then introduce a Virasoro-inspired ansatz, which becomes a set of nonlinear relations among Wilson coefficients and shrinks the allowed region toward the Virasoro-Shapiro trajectory. Finally, we study a gravity-pole-subtracted setup, where the regular part of the amplitude has a well-defined forward limit. In this stripped problem, the nonlinear constraints reduce the allowed region to a small island containing the Virasoro-Shapiro point, for which we provide an analytic bootstrap explanation.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the dispersive S-matrix bootstrap to constrain the low-energy expansion of the ten-dimensional Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude, imposing analyticity, crossing, unitarity, and Regge behavior; it introduces a Virasoro-inspired ansatz that yields nonlinear Wilson coefficient relations, and in a gravity-pole-subtracted setup, isolates the Virasoro-Shapiro solution as a unique island with an analytic explanation.
AI.motivation: To non-perturbatively constrain the low-energy effective action of string theory—specifically the Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude—using fundamental S-matrix principles without relying on worldsheet constructions.
AI.method: Dispersive S-matrix bootstrap: constructs dispersion relations from analyticity and Regge boundedness; enforces crossing symmetry via null constraints; imposes partial-wave unitarity; introduces a Virasoro-inspired ansatz encoding nonlinear relations among Wilson coefficients; analyzes both full and gravity-pole-subtracted amplitudes.
AI.result: Numerical bounds on normalized low-energy coefficients (e.g., $c_2$, $c_3$) are derived; the Virasoro-inspired ansatz significantly shrinks the allowed parameter space; in the pole-subtracted setup, the constraints confine the solution to a small island containing the exact Virasoro-Shapiro point, with analytic justification via forward-limit consistency and crossing-symmetric dispersion.
AI.conclusion: The Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude is highly constrained—and effectively singled out—by fundamental S-matrix principles alone, supporting the idea that stringy UV completions are privileged by consistency conditions beyond effective field theory.
